Option of the segment in the Folders row of the Index page: read everything on the computer. Not available yet; the option is dimmed.
Option of the segment in the Folders row of the Index page: read only the folders listed below.
Dim sentence under the title of the Folders row of the Index page: only the folders listed below are read; the option Everything (the whole computer) is dimmed and comes in a later version.
strings.en: Only the folders below are read. Reading the whole computer comes in a later version.
strings.de: Gelesen werden nur die Ordner unten. Den ganzen Computer lesen kommt in einer späteren Version.

strings.context: Warning under a folder line on the Index and Hermes pages: the folder is on a drive that is not connected right now.
Button under the folder list of the Index and Hermes pages: opens the system folder dialog to add a folder. The plus sign belongs to the label.
Line on the Index page when no folder is listed.
strings.en: No folder yet. The index only reads folders you add.
strings.de: Noch kein Ordner. Der Index liest nur Ordner, die du hinzufügst.

strings.context: Index page of the settings: line under the folders that are sources or targets of filing. They are listed there only to be seen and are changed on the Filing page, see the button beside it.
strings.en: Sources and targets are read too. They are changed on the Sorting page.
strings.de: Quellen und Ziele werden mitgelesen. Geändert werden sie unter Einsortieren.

strings.context: Index page of the settings: button beside the line about sources and targets; it shows the Filing page of the settings.
Label of the row of the Index page about reading scans and photos with the recognizer the operating system brings (macOS Vision). Only shown on macOS.
Description under the row about reading scans and photos on the Index page. macOS Vision is the name of Apple's recognizer.
State shown at the right of a row of the Index page: the function is ready to use. One word.
Label of the row of the Index page about the second text recognizer that ncrs downloads.
Description under the row about the fallback recognizer on the Index page. It consists of 2 files of 40 MB together.
strings.en: Steps in when macOS cannot read a page. 2 files, 40 MB. The only recognizer on Linux and Windows.
strings.de: Springt ein, wenn macOS eine Seite nicht lesen kann. 2 Dateien, 40 MB. Auf Linux und Windows der einzige Erkenner.

strings.context: Second line under the AI model row of the Index page of the settings tab when the model is in memory. Takes the file name, the memory it uses with its unit (for example 2.5 GB) and what it computes on: the name of the graphics device, or the word for the processor.
Part of the second line under the AI model row of the Index page: the model computes on the processor, not on a graphics card. Follows the words 'runs on'.
Second line under the AI model row of the Index page when the model file could not be used. Takes the reason, which is English and stays untranslated.
Description under the row about the AI model on this computer on the AI page. Qwen3.5-4B is the name of the model.
strings.en: Qwen3.5-4B. Without a model only file names and dates.
strings.de: Qwen3.5-4B. Ohne Modell nur Dateinamen und Datum.

strings.context: State of the AI model on the AI page while the Hermes switch there is off. Short phrase; Hermes is the name of the filing assistant.
State of the AI model on the Index page: the model is not on this computer.
State of the AI model on the Index page: the model is being downloaded right now.
State of the AI model on the Index page: the model is on this computer and ready. One word.
State of the AI on the Index page: an own server is used instead of the local model. {model} is the model name on that server.
State of the AI on the Index page: it could not start. The reason is on the status page.
State of the AI on the Index page: it was switched on and starts when ncrs is started the next time.
Description under the rows of own names, accounts and tax numbers on the Index page. The typed text is added with the plus button or Enter.
strings.en: Several allowed: separate them with commas or semicolons.
strings.de: Mehrere möglich: mit Komma oder Semikolon trennen.

strings.context: Button next to the field of an own detail (name, account, tax number) on the Index page: adds what is typed. A plus sign.
Row on the Index page. {documents} is how many documents the index holds, {understood} how many of them the AI has read and sorted.
Description under the row with the document counts on the Index page.
strings.en: The rest runs in the background.

strings.context: Button on the Index page that pauses the background work of the index. Verb.
Button on the Index page that continues the paused background work of the index. Verb.
Label of the row of the Index page that chooses how much of the computer the index may use. Noun.
Description under the Load row on the Index page.
strings.en: How much of your computer the index may use.
strings.de: Wie viel Rechner der Index nehmen darf.

strings.context: Option of the Load segment on the Index page: use little, so the computer stays usable.
Option of the Load segment on the Index page: use a moderate share.
Option of the Load segment on the Index page: use all the computer can give.
Row on the Index page. {count} is how many files could not be read; at least 2.
Row on the Index page when exactly one file could not be read.
Button in the row of unreadable files on the Index page: opens the list of the files and why they could not be read. Verb.

Description under the Hermes switch at the top of the AI page of the settings tab. Off: Hermes watches no sources and asks no AI model for sorting documents, the chat, rename suggestions or learning rules.
strings.en: Off: no folders watched, no model asked.
strings.de: Aus: keine Ordner beobachtet, kein Modell gefragt.

strings.context: Option of the segment at the top of the AI page: Hermes works. One word.
Option of the segment at the top of the AI page: Hermes watches no folders and calls no AI model. One word.
Button in the Order section of the Hermes page after all areas are shown: shows only the first three again.
Heading of the section of the Hermes page about the saved chats with Hermes. Plural noun.
Row of the Hermes page: after how long old chats of the Hermes chat are deleted, counted from the last time a chat was used. The choices are at the right.
Note under the row about deleting old chats on the Hermes page: when it happens.
strings.en: Old chats are deleted when ncrs starts.
strings.de: Alte Chats werden beim Start von ncrs gelöscht.

strings.context: Choice of the row about deleting old chats on the Hermes page: chats are never deleted by age. One word.
Choice of the row about deleting old chats on the Hermes page: chats unused for 30 days are deleted.
Choice of the row about deleting old chats on the Hermes page: chats unused for 90 days are deleted.
Line under the History heading on the Hermes page when Hermes has not filed anything yet.
Line of the last run in the History section. {when} is a date and time such as Today 14:02, {count} the number of files (at least 2), {from} the folder they came from.
Line of the last run in the History section when it filed exactly one file. {when} is a date and time, {from} the folder the file came from.
Button on the run in the History section: puts the files of the run back. Verb phrase.
Notice when the last run could not be put back. {reason} is the system's explanation.
strings.en: The last run could not be undone: {reason}
strings.de: Der letzte Lauf konnte nicht rückgängig gemacht werden: {reason}

strings.context: Notice after a run was put back but some files stayed where Hermes had put them, because they changed or their old place is taken. {left} is a number.
strings.en: Run undone, but {left} files stayed where they are: they changed or their old place is taken.
strings.de: Lauf rückgängig gemacht, aber {left} Dateien sind geblieben: Sie haben sich geändert oder ihr alter Platz ist belegt.

strings.context: Notice on the Index page when the numbers of the index could not be read, so the page shows nothing instead of the real figures. {reason} is the system's explanation.
strings.en: The index could not be read: {reason}
strings.de: Der Index konnte nicht gelesen werden: {reason}

strings.context: Reason inside the notices that the index could not be read or the last run could not be undone, when the work in the background ended without an answer. Short clause, no full stop.
strings.en: the work in the background stopped unexpectedly
strings.de: die Arbeit im Hintergrund ist unerwartet abgebrochen

strings.context: Title of the question before a downloaded model is deleted from this computer.
Question before the fallback text recognizer is deleted from this computer.
strings.en: Remove the fallback recognizer from this Mac? You can load it again later.
strings.de: Den Ersatz-Erkenner von diesem Mac entfernen? Du kannst ihn später wieder laden.

strings.context: Question before the AI model is deleted from this computer.
strings.en: Remove the AI model from this Mac? You can load it again later.
strings.de: Das KI-Modell von diesem Mac entfernen? Du kannst es später wieder laden.

strings.context: Notice when a model could not be deleted. {reason} is the system's explanation.
strings.en: The model could not be removed: {reason}
strings.de: Das Modell konnte nicht entfernt werden: {reason}

strings.context: Description under a folder of the Index page. {path} is where the folder is, {count} how many documents the index holds from it; at least 2.
Description under a folder of the Index page when the index holds exactly one document from it. {path} is where the folder is.
Label of the row of the Index page that shows whether the index is encrypted. Noun.
Day word in a run line of the History section on the Hermes page, followed by the time: Today 14:02.
Day word in a run line of the History section on the Hermes page, followed by the time: Yesterday 09:30.

Run line of the history on the sorting page when the folder the files went to is known. {line} is the line up to the source folder, for example: Today 14:02 · 12 files from Downloads. {to} is the target folder.
Description under a run of the History section: some of the folders the files went to. {folders} is a comma separated list of paths.
Button under the last runs of the History section on the Hermes page: lists all runs that are kept.
Button in the row of a rule or a report on the settings pages Rules and Reports: opens the small dialog to change it.
Title of the dialog in which an existing rule is changed on the Rules page of the settings.
Entry of the feature list on the settings tab: how the Monitor page measures and shows the machine.
Line under the heading of the Monitor page on the settings tab. The Monitor page lists CPU, memory, drives, network and running tasks.
strings.en: What the Monitor page measures, how often, and what the status bar shows of it.
strings.de: Was die Seite Monitor misst, wie oft, und was die Statusleiste davon zeigt.

strings.context: Entry of the feature list on the settings tab: the page about the installed version of ncrs, the check for a newer one and how to install it.
Line under the heading of the Updates page on the settings tab. The page shows the installed version, the switch of the daily check and, when a newer version exists, how to get it.
strings.en: The installed version, whether ncrs looks for a newer one, and how to install it.
strings.de: Die installierte Version, ob ncrs nach einer neueren sucht, und wie man sie installiert.

strings.context: Label of the row that sets how often the Monitor page measures the machine, on the settings tab.
Label of the row that sets how the tasks on the Monitor page are sorted at first, on the settings tab.
Label of the row that sets the unit of the network speed on the Monitor page, on the settings tab.
Label of the row that sets whether the drive list on the Monitor page shows used or free space, on the settings tab.
Label of the on/off switch that puts the CPU load in the status bar, on the settings tab.
Label of the on/off switch that puts the memory use in the status bar, on the settings tab.
Label of the on/off switch that puts the swap use in the status bar, on the settings tab.
Label of the on/off switch that puts the load average in the status bar, on the settings tab. Not offered on Windows.
Label of the on/off switch that puts the network speed in the status bar, on the settings tab.
Label of the row that sets whether the status bar shows numbers or symbols for the chosen values, on the settings tab.
Label of the row that sets whether network interfaces without traffic are listed on the Monitor page, on the settings tab.
Label of the row that sets whether system volumes are listed among the drives on the Monitor page, on the settings tab.
Choice of the refresh row on the settings tab: measure every second.
Choice of the refresh row on the settings tab: measure every two seconds.
Choice of the refresh row on the settings tab: measure every five seconds.
Choice of the task sort row on the settings tab: by processor use.
Choice of the task sort row on the settings tab: by memory use.
Choice of the task sort row on the settings tab: by the processor time a task has used.
Choice of the network speed row on the settings tab: speed in bytes per second.
Choice of the network speed row on the settings tab: speed in bits per second.
Choice of the drive column row on the settings tab: show the used space.
Choice of the drive column row on the settings tab: show the free space.
Choice of the status bar style row on the settings tab: percentages and speeds as numbers.
Choice of the status bar style row on the settings tab: a small bar symbol instead of a number.
Choice of a visibility row on the Monitor page settings: do not list these entries.
Choice of a visibility row on the Monitor page settings: list these entries.

Entry of the command palette that runs the key action system_monitor, which opens the Monitor page with the load of the computer. The plain name of what the action does, as short as a menu entry; the key bound to it is shown beside it.
Name of the Monitor page: the mode field in its status bar and the tab in the title bar.
The mode field at the left end of the status bar of the Monitor page, in capitals like the one of the settings tab. The same word as the page's name.
Shown on the Monitor page until the first measurement of the computer has arrived.
Header of the Monitor page: how long the computer has been running. {time} is a duration such as 3d 4h.
Title of the processor meter at the top of the Monitor page.
Title of the main memory meter at the top of the Monitor page.
Title of the swap meter at the top of the Monitor page; swap is memory spilled to disk.
Title of the load average meter on the Monitor page. Not shown on Windows.
Line under the processor meter. {brand} is the processor model, {cores} the number of cores.
Line under the memory meter. Placeholders are sizes such as 8.2G.
Line under the swap meter. Placeholders are sizes such as 1.5G.
Line under the load meter: the load average over one, five and fifteen minutes.
Heading of the network block on the Monitor page, which lists the network interfaces.
Column title in the network block of the Monitor page: the name of the interface.
Column title in the network block of the Monitor page: data received per second.
Column title in the network block of the Monitor page: data sent per second.
Heading of the drives block on the Monitor page, which lists mounted volumes.
Column title in the drives block of the Monitor page: space in use.
Column title in the drives block of the Monitor page: space still free.
Column title in the drives block of the Monitor page: size of the volume.
Column title in the drives block of the Monitor page: data read per second.
Column title in the drives block of the Monitor page: data written per second.
Heading of the block on the Monitor page that lists temperature sensors.
Heading of the task list on the Monitor page, which lists running programs.
Line next to the task list heading. {running}, {sleeping} and {other} are counts; {sort} is the name of the column the list is sorted by.
Hint in the empty filter field above the task list on the Monitor page. {key} is the shortcut that focuses it.
Column title of the task list on the Monitor page: share of processor time in percent.
Column title of the task list on the Monitor page: share of main memory in percent.
Column title of the task list on the Monitor page: resident memory in bytes.
Column title of the task list on the Monitor page: the process number.
Column title of the task list on the Monitor page: the owner of the task.
Column title of the task list on the Monitor page: processor time the task has used.
Column title of the task list on the Monitor page: one letter for running or sleeping.
Column title of the task list on the Monitor page: the command line of the task.
Context menu entry of a task on the Monitor page: ends the task after a confirmation.
Context menu entry of a task on the Monitor page: copies its command line to the clipboard.
Context menu entry of a task on the Monitor page: shows the folder of its program in the active panel.
Title of the confirmation dialog for ending a task on the Monitor page.
Line in the kill dialog naming the task. {name} is the program, {pid} its process number.
Warning in the kill dialog: the task ends at once and unsaved work in it is lost.
strings.en: The task ends at once. Unsaved work in it is lost.
strings.de: Der Prozess wird sofort beendet. Nicht gespeicherte Arbeit darin geht verloren.

strings.context: Button of the kill dialog that ends the task.
Hint in the middle of the status bar of the Monitor page while every process has its own row. g is the key; it groups the processes by program.
Hint in the middle of the status bar of the Monitor page while processes of one program are shown as one row. g is the key; it shows every process again.
Right side of the status bar of the Monitor page: how often it measures. {seconds} is a number.
Error in the status bar of the Monitor page: the task is ncrs itself and is not ended. {name} is the program.
strings.en: {name} is ncrs itself and cannot be killed
strings.de: {name} ist ncrs selbst und kann nicht beendet werden

strings.context: Error in the status bar of the Monitor page: the task has ended or the number belongs to another task now. {name} is the program.
strings.en: {name} is gone or has changed, nothing was killed
strings.de: {name} ist beendet oder ein anderer Prozess, nichts wurde beendet

strings.context: Error in the status bar of the Monitor page: the system did not let the task end. {name} is the program.
Error in the status bar of the Monitor page: the measurement failed. {reason} is the system's message.
Notice in the status bar of the Monitor page after a task ended. {name} is the program.
Tooltip of the CPU and memory text at the right end of the status bar; a click opens the Monitor page.
Notice in the status bar after the command line of a task from the Monitor page was copied to the clipboard.

Entry of the command palette and the File menu that runs the key action open_terminal: starts the user's terminal in the folder of the active panel, or in the folder under the cursor. Imperative, as short as a menu entry; the key bound to it is shown beside it.
Entry of the context menu: starts the user's terminal in the folder under the cursor, or in the folder of the panel when the cursor is on a file. Verb, imperative.

Status bar notice when 'Open terminal here' is used while the active panel shows a server, the inside of an archive or a list of search hits: there is no folder on this computer to start a terminal in.
strings.en: A terminal needs a folder on this computer
strings.de: Ein Terminal braucht einen Ordner auf diesem Computer

strings.context: Status bar error when 'Open terminal here' finds no terminal on the computer and none is set in the settings.
strings.en: No terminal found. Choose one under Settings > Programs.
strings.de: Kein Terminal gefunden. Wähle eines unter Einstellungen > Programme.

strings.context: Status bar error when the terminal could not be started. Takes the folder name and the OS reason.
strings.en: Could not open a terminal in {name}: {reason}
strings.de: Terminal in {name} konnte nicht geöffnet werden: {reason}

strings.context: Error in the connect dialog when the server ended the connection setup without showing a host key, so it cannot be checked. Takes the host.
strings.en: {host} did not show a host key, so the server cannot be checked
strings.de: {host} hat keinen Hostschlüssel gezeigt, der Server lässt sich daher nicht prüfen

strings.context: Reason shown inside the failure text of the connect dialog when the user trusts a new host key but ncrs has no file to keep it in (no home folder known). Short, without a full stop.
strings.en: there is no file to keep the host key in
strings.de: es gibt keine Datei, in der der Hostschlüssel gespeichert werden kann

strings.context: Name of a setting on the programs page: the terminal that 'Open terminal here' starts. One word, noun.
Explanation under the terminal setting: Automatic means the first terminal found on the computer; in an own command, {path} is replaced by the folder.
strings.en: Automatic takes the first terminal found. In your own command {path} stands for the folder.
strings.de: Automatisch nimmt das erste gefundene Terminal. Im eigenen Befehl steht {path} für den Ordner.

strings.context: Name of an on/off switch on the programs page, Windows only: ncrs is added to the right-click menu of folders and files in the Explorer.
strings.en: Show in the Explorer context menu

strings.context: Explanation under the Explorer context menu switch on the programs page (Windows only).
strings.en: Adds "Open in ncrs" to the right-click menu of folders, of the folder background and of files.
strings.de: Fügt „In ncrs öffnen“ zum Rechtsklick-Menü von Ordnern, Ordnerhintergrund und Dateien hinzu.

strings.context: Name of an on/off switch on the programs page (Windows and Linux only): ncrs is the program that opens folders when another program or the system asks for the folder manager.
strings.en: ncrs as the default file manager

strings.context: Explanation under the default file manager switch on the programs page. Turning it off gives folders back to the program that opened them before.
strings.en: Folders other programs open go to ncrs. Turning this off goes back to the earlier choice.
strings.de: Ordner, die andere Programme öffnen, gehen an ncrs. Beim Ausschalten gilt wieder die frühere Wahl.

strings.context: Dim info line at the end of the programs page on macOS, where the switches of the other systems do not exist. Says where ncrs shows up as a program for folders and files. 'Open With' is the Finder menu entry, use the system's own name for it.
strings.en: On macOS, ncrs is listed in the Finder under “Open With” for folders and files.
strings.de: Auf macOS steht ncrs im Finder unter „Öffnen mit“ für Ordner und Dateien.

strings.context: Status message when the default file manager or Explorer menu switch on the programs page could not be changed. {reason} is the system's own error text.
The words of the ncrs entry in the Windows Explorer right-click menu. Starts with a verb; written into the registry when the switch is turned on.
Choice in the terminal list on the programs page: the first terminal found on the computer is used. Takes the name of that terminal.
Choice in the terminal list on the programs page when no terminal was found on the computer: the same 'Automatic' choice, without a name.
Choice in the terminal list on the programs page: the user types the program and its arguments themselves.
Placeholder in the empty field of the own terminal command on the programs page. An example line; {path} must stay as it is.
Chat reply when an opened folder holds no files. {folder} is its name. Followed by a suggested order and buttons.
strings.en: {folder} is empty. This order would be possible:
strings.de: {folder} ist leer. Möglich wäre diese Ordnung:

strings.context: Title of the card that lists the folder levels and file name Hermes found in a filing folder. {count} is the number of levels.
Title of the card that lists the folder levels after the user started to change them. Replaces the title of the levels found.
Title of the card with the standard order proposed for a new, empty filing folder. {count} is the number of levels.
Last line of the levels card. {fitting} files follow the found order, {total} files were checked.

Chat text under the levels card when the order the model recognised fits too few of the files. {fitting} of {total} files follow it. One button changes the levels, one suggests rules without this order.
strings.en: This order fits only {fitting} of {total} files. Change the levels, or let me suggest rules without this order.
strings.de: Diese Reihenfolge passt nur auf {fitting} von {total} Dateien. Ändere die Ebenen, oder lass dir Regeln ohne diese Reihenfolge vorschlagen.

strings.context: One line below the levels card for a file that does not follow the found order. {file} is its path, {written} is the path the order would give it.
One line below the levels card for a file the found order cannot write a path for. {file} is its path.
strings.en: {file} cannot be written by this order
strings.de: {file} lässt sich mit dieser Ordnung nicht schreiben

strings.context: Button under the levels Hermes found: the levels are right.
Button: take the levels shown for an empty folder.
Button: change the levels shown.
Button: use the standard order year, then date_sender_kind as file name.
Button under the levels card after the user changed a level in words: take the levels as they now stand and go on to the rule suggestions.
Button under the levels card after a change: say one more change of the levels in words.
Button under the levels card after a change: throw the changes away and show the levels Hermes found again.
Button while the user changes the levels: nothing more to change, take the levels as they stand and go on to the rule suggestions. Always there, also before the first change.
Small line under a changed level in the levels card. {value} is what the level wrote before the change, from a real file.
Line under the levels card after a change when every existing file already fits the changed levels.
strings.en: Every existing file already fits these levels.
strings.de: Alle vorhandenen Dateien passen schon zu diesen Ebenen.

strings.context: Chat reply when the user names only a level number while changing the levels; asks what should be different on that level. {level} is the number as on the card.
strings.en: What should be different about level {level}?
strings.de: Was soll an Ebene {level} anders sein?

strings.context: Explains how to change the levels: tell it in a typed sentence; the buttons below finish. Examples with level numbers as on the card.
strings.en: Tell me in words what to change, for example "year and month together in level 2" or "date first in level 3". Say when you are done.
strings.de: Sag in Worten, was sich ändern soll, zum Beispiel „Jahr und Monat zusammen in Ebene 2“ oder „Datum vorne bei Ebene 3“. Sag Bescheid, wenn du fertig bist.

strings.context: Role of a folder level whose name is the same for all files: it stays as it is.
Role of the last level, the file name. {parts} are the fields it is made of.
Name of the day field in the levels card, one word.
Name of the recipient field in the levels card, one word.
Role of the file name when Hermes makes it automatically.
Header of the list in the changed-levels card of the files that would have another path under the changed levels. Nothing is renamed. {count} is how many.
Last line under the example lines of the rule trial when more documents would move than are shown. {count} is how many are not shown.
Chat reply when the typed words gave no usable order of levels.
strings.en: I could not make an order from that. Try again in other words?
strings.de: Daraus konnte ich keine Ordnung machen. Sag es nochmal anders?

strings.context: Entry of the command palette and of the menus that runs the key action permissions: opens the dialog that shows and changes the access rights of the selected files. Menus add the ellipsis themselves. One word, plural noun.
Name of the icon column in the column menu of a panel header and in the settings page for columns. The column shows a small picture before the file name. One word, noun.
Column header above the date a file was created. One word; may expand in some languages.
Column header above the kind of a file in words (folder, image, PDF). One word, noun.
Column header above the file name extension, the part after the last dot. One word, noun.
Column header above the access rights of a file (rwxr-xr-x; read-only, hidden, system on Windows). One word, plural noun.
Column header above the user who owns a file. Not shown on Windows. One word, noun.
Column header above the group that owns a file. Not shown on Windows. One word, noun.
Column header above the date a file was last read. One word; may expand in some languages.
Column header above the place a link points to; empty for everything that is not a link. Short, noun.
Note beside the Name entry in the column menu that opens from a panel header. The name column cannot be switched off. One lowercase word.
Switch in the column menu of a panel header: when on, both panels show the same columns in the same order; when off, each panel has its own.
Entry at the bottom of the column menu of a panel header that opens the Columns page of the settings tab. The ellipsis shows that a page opens.
Entry at the bottom of the column menu of a panel header that puts the columns back to the built-in ones: icon, name, size, modified.
Value in the Type column of a file panel for a folder. One word, noun.
Value in the Type column of a file panel for a symbolic link or shortcut. One word, noun.
Value in the Type column of a file panel for a link whose target does not exist. Short noun phrase.
Value in the Type column of a file panel for a picture file such as PNG or JPEG. One word, noun.
Value in the Type column of a file panel for a video file. One word, noun.
Value in the Type column of a file panel for a sound or music file. One word, noun.
Value in the Type column of a file panel for a PDF file. The format name, keep it.
Value in the Type column of a file panel for a text document such as DOCX or ODT. One word, noun.
Value in the Type column of a file panel for a spreadsheet such as XLSX or CSV. One word, noun.
Value in the Type column of a file panel for a source code file. One word, noun.
Value in the Type column of a file panel for a program that can be run. One word, noun.
Value in the Type column of a file panel for a packed archive such as ZIP or TAR. One word, noun.
Value in the Type column of a file panel for a file of no known kind. One word, noun.
Entry of the feature list on the settings tab, in the group of the files: the page for the columns of the file panels. One word, plural noun.
Line under the heading of the Columns page on the settings tab.
strings.en: Which columns the panels show, in which order, and how dates and sizes look.
strings.de: Welche Spalten die Panels zeigen, in welcher Reihenfolge und wie Datum und Größe aussehen.

strings.context: Label of the row on the Columns page that sets whether both file panels show the same columns. One word, plural noun.
Note under the Panels row on the Columns page, explaining the two options of the segment.
strings.en: Both panels show the same columns, or each panel has its own.
strings.de: Beide Panels zeigen dieselben Spalten, oder jedes Panel hat seine eigenen.

strings.context: Option of the Panels segment on the Columns page: both panels show the same columns.
Option of the Panels segment on the Columns page: each panel has its own columns, a left and a right list.
Option of the segment on the Columns page that picks which list is edited while each panel has its own columns: the left panel.
Option of the segment on the Columns page that picks which list is edited while each panel has its own columns: the right panel.
Label of the row on the Columns page that lists every column with a switch and a handle to change the order.
Note under the Columns and order row. The arrows are the up and down buttons beside each column; the header is the title row of a file panel.
strings.en: ↑/↓ changes the order. The same works in the panel itself, by dragging at the column header.
strings.de: Mit ↑/↓ änderst du die Reihenfolge. Dasselbe geht im Panel direkt am Spaltenkopf durch Ziehen.

strings.context: Description beside the Icon column on the Columns page.
strings.en: Folder, link or kind of file as a picture before the name.
strings.de: Ordner, Link oder Dateiart als Bild vor dem Namen.

strings.context: Description beside the Name column on the Columns page. The name column cannot be switched off.
Description beside the Size column on the Columns page. <DIR> is the marker shown for a folder and is not translated; Space is the key that computes the size of a folder.
strings.en: Folders show <DIR>; Space computes the folder size.
strings.de: Bei Ordnern <DIR>, mit Leertaste die Ordnergröße.

strings.context: Description beside the Modified column on the Columns page.
strings.en: When the content was last changed.
strings.de: Wann der Inhalt zuletzt geändert wurde.

strings.context: Description beside the Permissions column on the Columns page. rwxr-xr-x is the Unix notation and stays; the three words on Windows are the attributes of a file there.
strings.en: rwxr-xr-x. On Windows: Read-only, Hidden, System.
strings.de: rwxr-xr-x. Unter Windows: Schreibgeschützt, Versteckt, System.

strings.context: Description beside the Created column on the Columns page.
strings.en: When the file was created. Not every file system knows this.
strings.de: Wann die Datei angelegt wurde. Nicht jedes Dateisystem kennt das.

strings.context: Description beside the Type column on the Columns page.
strings.en: The kind of file in words: PDF, image, folder, link.
strings.de: Dateiart in Worten: PDF, Bild, Ordner, Link.

strings.context: Description beside the Extension column on the Columns page.
strings.en: The part after the last dot.
strings.de: Der Teil nach dem letzten Punkt.

strings.context: Description beside the Owner column and beside the Group column on the Columns page.
Description beside the Accessed column on the Columns page.
strings.en: When the file was last read. Many file systems do not keep it up to date.
strings.de: Letzter Lesezugriff. Viele Dateisysteme halten es nicht aktuell.

strings.context: Description beside the Link target column on the Columns page.
strings.en: Where a link points; empty for everything else.
strings.de: Wohin ein Link zeigt; leer bei allem anderen.

strings.context: Heading over the rows on the Columns page that set how dates and sizes are written. One word, plural noun.
Label of the row on the Columns page that sets how dates are written in the panels. One word, noun.
Note under the Date row on the Columns page: the three formats with an example each. Keep the three format names in step with the options of the segment.
strings.en: Relative: 5 min ago, yesterday 16:12. Short: Nov 5 16:12, with the year for dates before this year. ISO: 2026-11-05 16:12.
strings.de: Relativ: vor 5 Min., gestern 16:12. Kurz: 05.11. 16:12, mit Jahr vor dem laufenden Jahr. ISO: 2026-11-05 16:12.

strings.context: Option of the Date segment on the Columns page: dates as time passed, such as 5 min ago.
Option of the Date segment on the Columns page: day and month, the year only for older dates.
Option of the Date segment on the Columns page: year-month-day as in ISO 8601. The standard's name, keep it.
Label of the row on the Columns page that sets how sizes are written in the panels. One word, noun.
Note under the Size row on the Columns page: the three formats with an example each, for the same file.
strings.en: Bytes: 1433600 B. KB: 1400 KB. Readable: 1.4 MB.
strings.de: Bytes: 1433600 B. KB: 1400 KB. Lesbar: 1,4 MB.

strings.context: Option of the Size segment on the Columns page: the exact number of bytes. The unit name, keep it.
Option of the Size segment on the Columns page: always in kilobytes. The unit symbol, keep it.
Option of the Size segment on the Columns page: the unit that fits the size, such as 1.4 MB.
Relative date in a file panel for a time less than an hour ago. {n} is the number of minutes. Keep it short, it must fit a narrow column.
Relative date in a file panel for a time less than a day ago. {n} is the number of hours. Keep it short, it must fit a narrow column.
Relative date in a file panel for a time yesterday. {time} is the time of day, such as 14:03.
chrono format pattern, keep the % codes. The Short date in a file panel for a time in this year: day and month, then the time. English example: Nov 5 16:12; German: 05.11. 16:12.
chrono format pattern, keep the % codes. The Short date in a file panel for a time before this year: day, month and year, without the time. English example: Nov 5 2025; German: 05.11.2025.
Label of the row on the Appearance page that sets the font of the whole window. One word, noun.
Note under the Font row on the Appearance page. System is the first option of the list. Monospace means every character is equally wide; the panel columns are measured in characters.
strings.en: System takes the system's monospace font. Monospace fonts only, because columns are measured in characters.
strings.de: System nimmt die Monospace-Schrift des Systems. Nur Monospace-Schriften, weil Spalten in Zeichen gerechnet werden.

strings.context: First entry of the font list on the Appearance page. {name} is the name of the monospace font the system uses.
Small note beside a font in the font list on the Appearance page: the font comes with ncrs and is not taken from the system. One lowercase word.
Label of the row on the Appearance page that sets the size of the text in the whole window. One word, noun.
Note under the Font size row on the Appearance page. System is the first option of the list; text scaling is the setting of the operating system that makes text larger or smaller.
strings.en: System takes the system's size times its text scaling. Everything grows with it: rows, spacing, icons.
strings.de: System nimmt die Größe des Systems mal dessen Textskalierung. Alles wächst mit: Zeilen, Abstände, Symbole.

strings.context: First entry of the font size list on the Appearance page. {size} is the size in points the system gives, after its text scaling.
Entry of the font size list on the Appearance page. {size} is a number of points.
Label of the row on the Appearance page that shows a small file panel in the chosen font and size. One word, noun.
Note under the Preview row on the Appearance page.
strings.en: This is how a panel looks in this font.
strings.de: So sieht ein Panel mit dieser Schrift aus.

strings.context: Title of the permissions dialog for one file or folder. {name} is its name.
Title of the permissions dialog for several entries. {parts} is the count of files, of folders, or both joined; a count of zero is left out.
Joins the count of files and the count of folders in the title of the permissions dialog. {files} and {folders} are already worded, e.g. '3 files' and '2 folders'.
Part of the title of the permissions dialog: several files. {count} is the number, two or more.
Part of the title of the permissions dialog: exactly one file.
Part of the title of the permissions dialog: several folders. {count} is the number, two or more.
Part of the title of the permissions dialog: exactly one folder.
Label of the row in the permissions dialog with the rights of the user who owns the file. One word, noun.
Label of the row in the permissions dialog with the rights of the group that owns the file. One word, noun.
Label of the row in the permissions dialog with the rights of everybody else. One or two words.
Label of the checkbox in the permissions dialog for the right to read a file or list a folder. One word, verb.
Label of the checkbox in the permissions dialog for the right to change a file or add to a folder. One word, verb.
Label of the checkbox in the permissions dialog for the right to run a file or enter a folder. One word, verb.
Line in the permissions dialog naming the owner and the group of the file. {owner} and {group} are account names.
Shown in a checkbox or beside it in the permissions dialog when the selected files differ in that right. One lowercase word.
Label of the field in the permissions dialog where the rights are typed as an octal number such as 755. One word.
Note beside the octal field in the permissions dialog: typing one number sets the rights of all selected files to the same.
strings.en: A number sets all of them alike

strings.context: Heading of the folded part of the permissions dialog with the options for the contents of folders. One word.
Label of the switch in the permissions dialog: the change also goes to everything inside the selected folders.
strings.en: Apply to the contents of folders
strings.de: Auf den Inhalt der Ordner anwenden

strings.context: Label of the row in the permissions dialog that says what happens to the files inside the selected folders. Plural noun, one word.
Label of the row in the permissions dialog that says what happens to the folders inside the selected folders. Plural noun, one word.
Option for the contents of folders in the permissions dialog: they get the same rights as set above.
Option for files inside folders in the permissions dialog: the rights as set above, but without the right to execute.
Option for the contents of folders in the permissions dialog: their rights stay as they are.
Note under the checkboxes of the permissions dialog. A dash is the third state of a checkbox: the selected files differ in that right. The change runs in the background like copying.
strings.en: Only boxes you click change; a dash stays as it is on each file. Runs in the background like copying, with progress and cancel.
strings.de: Nur angeklickte Häkchen ändern sich, ein Strich bleibt, wie er bei jeder Datei ist. Läuft im Hintergrund wie Kopieren, mit Fortschritt und Abbrechen.

strings.context: Label of the checkbox in the permissions dialog on Windows for the read-only attribute of a file.
Note in the permissions dialog on Windows, where there are no owner, group and others rights and only the read-only attribute can be changed.
strings.en: On Windows only read-only can be changed here.
strings.de: Unter Windows lässt sich hier nur Schreibgeschützt ändern.

strings.context: Text of the progress bar of a running permissions change. {done} is how many entries are done, {total} how many there are.
Label of the checkbox for the setuid bit in the advanced part of the permissions dialog. Technical term, usually kept as is.
Label of the checkbox for the setgid bit in the advanced part of the permissions dialog. Technical term, usually kept as is.
Label of the checkbox for the sticky bit in the advanced part of the permissions dialog. Technical term, usually kept as is.
Status bar notice after a permissions change. {count} is the number of entries whose rights were changed.
Status bar notice when a permissions change could not be applied to some entries. {count} is how many, {reason} the system's reason for the first.
Button of the permissions dialog that applies the rights. One word, verb.
Entry of the command palette that runs the key action open_favourite_1: opens the first favourite in the active panel. The key bound to it is shown beside it.
Entry of the command palette that runs the key action open_favourite_2: opens the second favourite in the active panel. The key bound to it is shown beside it.
Entry of the command palette that runs the key action open_favourite_3: opens the third favourite in the active panel. The key bound to it is shown beside it.
Entry of the command palette that runs the key action open_favourite_4: opens the fourth favourite in the active panel. The key bound to it is shown beside it.
Entry of the command palette that runs the key action open_favourite_5: opens the fifth favourite in the active panel. The key bound to it is shown beside it.
Entry of the command palette that runs the key action open_favourite_6: opens the sixth favourite in the active panel. The key bound to it is shown beside it.
Entry of the command palette that runs the key action open_favourite_7: opens the seventh favourite in the active panel. The key bound to it is shown beside it.
Entry of the command palette that runs the key action open_favourite_8: opens the eighth favourite in the active panel. The key bound to it is shown beside it.
Entry of the command palette that runs the key action open_favourite_9: opens the ninth favourite in the active panel. The key bound to it is shown beside it.

Entry of the command palette and the menu that runs the key action tag_by_pattern: asks for a pattern of file names (* and ?, several separated by semicolons) and tags every row of the active panel that matches. The key bound to it is shown beside it.

Entry of the command palette and the menu that runs the key action untag_by_pattern: asks for a pattern of file names (* and ?, several separated by semicolons) and takes the tag off every row of the active panel that matches. The key bound to it is shown beside it.

Entry of the command palette and the menu that runs the key action go_to_path: opens a small dialog with one field for a typed or pasted path, which the active panel then opens. Imperative, as short as a menu entry.
Title of the dialog that asks for a pattern of file names and tags the rows of the active panel that match. Imperative, matches the other dialog titles.

Label next to the text field of the tag-by-pattern and untag-by-pattern dialogs. The field holds a pattern of file names: * stands for any characters, ? for one character, several patterns are separated by semicolons, upper and lower case do not matter. One or two words, no colon.
Confirm button in the tag-by-pattern dialog. Verb, what the button does.
Title of the dialog that asks for a pattern of file names and takes the tag off the rows of the active panel that match. Imperative, matches the other dialog titles.
Confirm button in the untag-by-pattern dialog. Verb, what the button does.

Title of the small dialog that Cmd+G (Ctrl+G on Linux and Windows) opens: one field for a path that is typed or pasted. Enter opens that folder in the active panel, or the folder of that file with the cursor on it. Imperative, matches the other dialog titles.
Label next to the text field of the Go to path dialog. The field holds the path of a folder or a file; a leading ~ stands for the home folder. One word, no colon.
Confirm button in the Go to path dialog. Verb, what the button does.
Entry of the menu of a slot of the favourites bar under the tabs: opens that favourite in the panel that is not active. Verb, imperative.
Entry of the menu of a slot of the favourites bar: moves the favourite one place to the left, so it gets a lower number. Verb, imperative.
Entry of the menu of a slot of the favourites bar: moves the favourite one place to the right, so it gets a higher number. Verb, imperative.
Last entry of the menu of a slot of the favourites bar: opens the Favourites page of the settings. The ellipsis belongs to the label.
Name of the folder of the installed programs (/Applications) on macOS, shown in the favourites bar and its overflow menu instead of the folder's English name on disk. Short, one word.
Tooltip of the button at the right end of the favourites bar under the path tabs. The bar shows as many favourites as fit; the button opens a menu with the others. Short, no full stop.
Entry of the feature list on the settings tab, in the group of the files: the page for the favourite folders. One word, plural noun.
Line under the heading of the Favourites page on the settings tab. The bar is the row of numbered favourites under the path tabs.
strings.en: Folders you reach in one step. As many as fit sit in the bar under the tabs, the rest in its menu.
strings.de: Ordner, die du in einem Schritt erreichst. So viele, wie passen, stehen in der Leiste unter den Tabs, der Rest in deren Menü.

strings.context: Entry of the feature list on the settings tab, in the group of the files: the page for the notes. One word, plural noun.
Line under the heading of the Notes page on the settings tab. Encryption and sync are about the notes tab.
strings.en: Where your notes live, a copy in a second folder, and encryption.
strings.de: Wo deine Notizen liegen, eine Kopie in einem zweiten Ordner und die Verschlüsselung.

strings.context: Heading of a section on the Notes page of the settings: where the notes are stored. Short, upper case in German is drawn by the program.
Heading of a section on the Notes page of the settings: the copy of the notes in a second folder, for example a cloud folder. Short.
Heading of a section on the Notes page of the settings: encrypting the notes with a key kept in the system's credential store. Short.
Heading of a section on the Notes page of the settings: what the assistant Hermes may do with the notes. Short, a name, not translated.
Row label on the Notes page of the settings: the folder the notes are stored in. Its value is shown beside it.
Note under the notes folder row on the Notes page of the settings: where the folder is changed. The config file is the file named config.toml.
strings.en: Set with the folder entry in [notes] of the config file.
strings.de: Wird mit dem Eintrag folder unter [notes] in der Konfigurationsdatei festgelegt.

strings.context: Row label on the Notes page of the settings: the second folder the notes are copied to, for example a folder of a cloud service. Empty means no sync.
Note under the sync folder row on the Notes page of the settings: type the path and press Enter; leave it empty to turn the sync off.
strings.en: Type the path and press Enter. Empty turns the sync off.
strings.de: Pfad eingeben und Enter drücken. Leer schaltet den Sync aus.

strings.context: Row label on the Notes page of the settings: which way the notes travel to the sync folder. The choices are 'One way' and 'Both ways'.
Note under the direction row on the Notes page of the settings: what each choice does. One way copies only, never deletes; both ways keeps both versions when a note changed on both sides.
strings.en: One way only copies new and changed notes and never deletes. Both ways keeps both versions when a note changed on both sides.
strings.de: Nur hin kopiert neue und geänderte Notizen und löscht nie. Beide Richtungen behält beide Fassungen, wenn eine Notiz auf beiden Seiten geändert wurde.

strings.context: Row label on the Notes page of the settings: when the sync runs by itself. The choices are after saving, at start and every few minutes.
Row label on the Notes page of the settings: when the notes were last synced, with the button that syncs now beside it.
Row label on the Notes page of the settings: a switch that makes every note encrypted, the existing ones and new ones.
Note under the encrypt-all row on the Notes page of the settings: encrypted notes are stored as .md.enc files and only readable after unlocking.
strings.en: Encrypted notes are stored as .md.enc files and open after you unlock them.
strings.de: Verschlüsselte Notizen liegen als .md.enc-Dateien vor und lassen sich nach dem Entsperren öffnen.

strings.context: Row label on the Notes page of the settings: after how long without input the key leaves memory and encrypted notes lock again.
Row label on the Notes page of the settings: the recovery key, a text that opens the encrypted notes on another computer. Shown on request.
Note under the recovery key row on the Notes page of the settings: keep it safe, anyone with it can read the encrypted notes.
strings.en: Keep it somewhere safe. Anyone who has it can read your encrypted notes.
strings.de: Bewahre ihn sicher auf. Wer ihn hat, kann deine verschlüsselten Notizen lesen.

strings.context: Row label on the Notes page of the settings: a field to type a recovery key into on a computer that has no key yet.
Note under the enter-recovery-key row on the Notes page of the settings: use it on a new computer, then press Enter.
strings.en: For a new computer. Paste the key and press Enter.
strings.de: Für einen neuen Computer. Schlüssel einfügen und Enter drücken.

strings.context: Row label on the Notes page of the settings: a switch that lets the assistant Hermes search, read and write notes. Encrypted notes only while unlocked.
strings.en: Hermes may read and write notes
strings.de: Hermes darf Notizen lesen und schreiben

strings.context: Note under the Hermes row on the Notes page of the settings: encrypted notes are left out while they are locked.
strings.en: Encrypted notes are left out while they are locked.
strings.de: Verschlüsselte Notizen bleiben außen vor, solange sie gesperrt sind.

strings.context: Choice on the Notes page of the settings, direction of the sync: notes only travel to the sync folder. Short, fits a button.
Choice on the Notes page of the settings, direction of the sync: notes travel both ways and the newer one wins. Short, fits a button.
Choice on the Notes page of the settings, when the sync runs: after every saved note. Short, fits a button.
Choice on the Notes page of the settings, when the sync runs: once when the program starts. Short, fits a button.
Choice on the Notes page of the settings, when the sync runs: every few minutes. {minutes} is the number of minutes. Short, fits a button.
Notes page of the settings: shown in place of the time of the last sync while a sync is running.
Notes page of the settings: shown in place of the time of the last sync when no sync has run since the program started.
Button on the Notes page of the settings that copies the notes to the sync folder at once. Verb, imperative.
Choice on the Notes page of the settings, lock timeout: the encrypted notes never lock by themselves. One word, fits a button.
Choice on the Notes page of the settings, lock timeout in minutes. {minutes} is the number. Short, fits a button.
Button on the Notes page of the settings that shows the recovery key. Verb, imperative, short.
Button on the Notes page of the settings that hides the recovery key again. Verb, imperative, short.
Notes page of the settings: placeholder shown in place of the recovery key while it is hidden. Dots, not a word.
Placeholder of the field on the Notes page of the settings where a recovery key is pasted on a computer that has no key yet.
Placeholder of the field on the Notes page of the settings where the path of the sync folder is typed.
Heading of the first group on the Favourites page: the settings of the bar under the path tabs. One word, noun.
Label of the switch on the Favourites page that shows or hides the favourites bar under the path tabs.
strings.en: Show the bar under the tabs

strings.context: Description of the switch for the favourites bar. {first} and {last} are the key chords that open the first and the ninth favourite, for example Cmd+1 and Cmd+9.
strings.en: {first} to {last} open the first nine. The keys can be changed under Keyboard shortcuts.
strings.de: {first} bis {last} öffnen die ersten neun. Die Tasten lassen sich unter Tastenkürzel ändern.

strings.context: Description of the switch for the favourites bar when the keys of the first nine favourites are not numbered one after the other.
strings.en: Keys open the first nine. They can be changed under Keyboard shortcuts.
strings.de: Tasten öffnen die ersten neun. Sie lassen sich unter Tastenkürzel ändern.

strings.context: Heading of the second group on the Favourites page: the list of favourite folders. One word, plural noun.
Sentence under the heading of the folder list on the Favourites page. {key} is the key chord that adds the current folder, for example Cmd+D.
strings.en: The order sets the number. {key} adds the folder you are in at the end.
strings.de: Die Reihenfolge bestimmt die Nummer. {key} fügt den Ordner, in dem du bist, am Ende an.

strings.context: Sentence under the heading of the folder list on the Favourites page when no key is bound to adding the current folder.
strings.en: The order sets the number. The add-favourite action puts the folder you are in at the end.
strings.de: Die Reihenfolge bestimmt die Nummer. Die Aktion Favorit hinzufügen fügt den Ordner, in dem du bist, am Ende an.

strings.context: Button in the row of a favourite on the Favourites page: moves the folder one place up the list. One word.
Button in the row of a favourite on the Favourites page: moves the folder one place down the list. One word.
Command and context menu entry, also the title of its first dialog: compares the folders shown in the left and the right panel and marks what differs. Verb phrase, imperative.
Column header above the comparison marks of a file panel while two folders are compared; it takes the place of the Hermes column. A noun.
Compare folders dialog: label before the folder of the left panel. One word.
Compare folders dialog: label before the folder of the right panel. One word.
Compare folders dialog: heading above the checkboxes that say what two files must have in common to count as the same file.
strings.en: Files count as the same when these match
strings.de: Dateien gelten als gleich, wenn diese übereinstimmen

strings.context: Compare folders dialog: checkbox. The modification dates of two files must match, within a couple of seconds. Otherwise the newer file is marked.
Compare folders dialog: checkbox. The content of two files of the same size must match.
Compare folders dialog: dim note under the Content checkbox. A server is an SFTP server the panel shows.
strings.en: Reads every file on both sides, so it takes longer. On a server it downloads them.
strings.de: Liest jede Datei auf beiden Seiten, das dauert länger. Auf einem Server werden sie heruntergeladen.

strings.context: Compare folders dialog: checkbox. The folders below the two folders are compared too; a folder is marked when something below it differs.
Compare folders dialog: the button that starts the comparison. Verb, imperative.
Bar above the panels while two folders are compared: its heading. A noun.
Compare bar: after a plus sign and a count, the entries that exist only in the left folder. Short, lowercase.
Compare bar: after an up triangle and a count, the files that are newer in the left folder. Short, lowercase.
Compare bar: after a plus sign and a count, the entries that exist only in the right folder. Short, lowercase.
Compare bar: after an up triangle and a count, the files that are newer in the right folder. Short, lowercase.
Compare bar: after an unequal sign and a count, the entries that differ without one being newer. Short, lowercase.
Compare bar: after an equals sign and a count, the entries that are the same on both sides. Short, lowercase.
Compare bar: checkbox. Both panels then show only the entries that are not the same.
Compare bar: button that copies what is missing or newer on the left to the right folder. The arrow points at the right; {count} is how many entries it copies.
Compare bar: button that copies what is missing or newer on the right to the left folder. The arrow points at the left; {count} is how many entries it copies.
Compare bar: button that compares the two folders again, with the same settings.
Compare bar: shown instead of the counts while the folders are being read and compared.
Status line when a folder could not be read during the comparison; the comparison ends and nothing is marked. {reason} is the system's explanation.
Compare column of a file panel: the entry exists only in this panel's folder. Starts with a plus sign.
Compare column of a file panel: the file is newer than the one in the other panel. Starts with an up triangle.
Compare column of a file panel: the file is older than the one in the other panel. Starts with a down triangle.
Compare column of a file panel: the entry exists on both sides and differs, without one being newer. Starts with an unequal sign.
Compare column of a file panel: the entry is the same on both sides. Starts with an equals sign.
Sync dialog title; {path} is the folder the entries are copied to.
Sync dialog: line under the title; {count} is how many entries are copied, {source} the folder they come from. The copy asks about files that already exist, as every copy does.
strings.en: {count} entries from {source}. Files that already exist are asked about, one by one or for all.
strings.de: {count} Einträge aus {source}. Bei Dateien, die es schon gibt, wird nachgefragt, einzeln oder für alle.

strings.context: Sync dialog: checkbox when syncing to the right. Off every time the dialog opens.
strings.en: Also delete on the right what is not on the left
strings.de: Auch rechts löschen, was links nicht da ist

strings.context: Sync dialog: checkbox when syncing to the left. Off every time the dialog opens.
strings.en: Also delete on the left what is not on the right
strings.de: Auch links löschen, was rechts nicht da ist

strings.context: Sync dialog, in the error color above the list of what would be deleted; {count} is how many entries, {path} the folder they are deleted from.
Sync dialog: dim note under the disabled delete checkbox, when the target folder is on a server or in an archive.
strings.en: Nothing is deleted on a server or in an archive.
strings.de: Auf einem Server oder in einem Archiv wird nichts gelöscht.

strings.context: Sync dialog: the button when the delete box is ticked; {copies} and {deletions} are counts of entries.
Sync dialog: the button when nothing is deleted; {copies} is the count of entries copied.
Viewer tab: the segment that shows a Markdown file formatted (headings, lists, links). Noun, short.
Viewer tab: the segment that shows the file as plain monospace text, the way it is on disk. Noun, short.
Viewer tab: button that opens the shown file in the program the system has for it. Verb, imperative.
Viewer tab: button that opens the shown file in the editor (key F4). Verb, imperative; the key cap is shown next to it.
Status line of the viewer tab while a Markdown file is shown. The keys are written as they are on the keyboard.
strings.en: Esc closes · ↑ ↓ PgUp PgDn scroll · Tab switches between rendered and source
strings.de: Esc schließt · ↑ ↓ Bild↑ Bild↓ blättern · Tab wechselt zwischen Ansicht und Quelltext

strings.context: Status line of the viewer tab while a file other than Markdown is shown. The keys are written as they are on the keyboard.
Notice when F3 meets a file too big for the viewer tab; it is opened with the system instead. {name} is the file name, {limit} the limit with its unit.
strings.en: {name} is larger than {limit}: opened with the system program instead.
strings.de: {name} ist größer als {limit}: stattdessen mit dem System geöffnet.

strings.context: Error when the viewer tab cannot read the file. {name} is the file name, {reason} the system's reason.
Entry of the command list that runs the key action notes: it opens the notes tab. Also the title of that tab, the name of the top of its tree and the key of its status bar. Noun, plural.

Entry of the command list and of the context menu of a file that runs the key action note_on_file: it opens the note that belongs to the file in the notes tab, made if there is none, ready to type. The shortcut is shown next to it.
Notes tab: placeholder of the search field above the tree; the search looks through the text of all notes.
Notes tab: button that makes a new note, and the title a new note starts with until its first line gives it one. Verb, imperative, short.
Notes tab: button that makes a new folder in the tree, and the name the new folder starts with. Short.

Notes tab: the made-up group in the tree that lists the notes on files, and the word before the path of the file in the line under a note's title. Kept short, in brackets, because it is not a folder on disk.
Notes tab: the segment that shows the note formatted (headings, lists, links). Noun, short.
Notes tab: the segment that puts the note in an editor, where it is saved while typing. Noun, short.
Notes tab: button on a note on a file that shows that file in the active panel. Verb, imperative.
Notes tab: part of the line under a note's title; {time} is the date and time the note was last changed.
Notes tab: what the right side says while no note is chosen.
strings.en: Choose a note or make a new one.
strings.de: Eine Notiz wählen oder eine neue anlegen.

strings.context: Notes tab: what the list says when the search finds no note.

Status line of the notes tab while a note is shown. Takes {key}, the key that starts a new note, spelled for the platform (e.g. ⌘N or Ctrl+N); keep {key} as is. The other keys are written as they are on the keyboard.
strings.en: {key} new note · Enter edits · Esc closes
strings.de: {key} neue Notiz · Enter bearbeitet · Esc schließt

strings.context: Status line of the notes tab while a note is edited.
strings.en: Saves while you type · Esc back to the view
strings.de: Speichert beim Tippen · Esc zurück zur Ansicht

strings.context: Status line of the notes tab while the search shows hits.
strings.en: Full text over all notes · Enter opens the hit
strings.de: Volltext über alle Notizen · Enter öffnet den Treffer

strings.context: Notes tab: shown in the status line when the notes folder cannot be read. {path} is the folder, {reason} the system's reason.
strings.en: The notes folder {path} cannot be used: {reason}
strings.de: Der Notizen-Ordner {path} lässt sich nicht verwenden: {reason}

strings.context: Error when a note or a folder of the notes cannot be written. {reason} is the system's reason with the path.
strings.de: Die Notiz lässt sich nicht speichern: {reason}

strings.context: Error line in the notes tab: the file of a note was changed outside the program while it was open, so the program did not overwrite it and saved the user's version as a second note next to it. {name} is the title of that second note.
strings.en: The note was changed outside ncrs. Your version was saved as "{name}" next to it.
strings.de: Die Notiz wurde außerhalb von ncrs geändert. Deine Fassung wurde als „{name}“ daneben gespeichert.

strings.context: Notes tab: word in brackets after the title of the copy that keeps the user's version when the note was changed outside the program, as in 'Shopping list (conflict)'. One word, lower case in English, no brackets.
Error line in the notes tab: the note for a file cannot be made because a file is already where it would go and the program cannot read it as a note. The file is left untouched. {path} is that file.
strings.en: The note for this file was not made: {path} exists and is not a note ncrs can read. It was left as it is.
strings.de: Die Notiz zu dieser Datei wurde nicht angelegt: {path} existiert und ist keine Notiz, die ncrs lesen kann. Sie wurde nicht verändert.

strings.context: Error line when the user quits while the Hermes index is being encrypted or started over, or while its recovery key is still on screen. Quitting now would lose the recovery key. Quitting again ends the program.
strings.en: The recovery key of the Hermes index is not saved yet. Quit again to leave without it.
strings.de: Der Wiederherstellungsschlüssel des Hermes-Index ist noch nicht gesichert. Noch einmal beenden verlässt das Programm ohne ihn.

strings.context: Error line when the user quits while a note could not be written. Quitting again ends the program and drops the unsaved text. {reason} is the system's reason with the path.
strings.en: A note could not be saved: {reason}. Quit again to discard it.
strings.de: Eine Notiz konnte nicht gespeichert werden: {reason}. Noch einmal beenden verwirft sie.

strings.context: Notes tab: line in the tree while the notes folder is being read for the first time.
Notes tab: line in the tree when the notes folder holds no note yet. 'New note' is the name of the button above the tree.
strings.en: No notes yet. Use "New note" to make one.
strings.de: Noch keine Notizen. Mit „Neue Notiz“ legst du eine an.

strings.context: Notes tab: entry of the menu on a note or folder in the tree (right click) that encrypts it. Verb, imperative, short.
Notes tab: entry of the menu on an encrypted note or folder in the tree (right click) that turns the encryption off for it. Verb, imperative, short.
Notes tab: entry of the menu in the tree that takes the key out of memory at once, so encrypted notes are locked until the next unlock. Verb, imperative, short.
Notes tab: line on the page of an encrypted note while the key is not in memory. The button 'Unlock' is below it; the system may ask for the computer password then.
strings.en: This note is encrypted. Unlock it to read and edit it.
strings.de: Diese Notiz ist verschlüsselt. Entsperre sie, um sie zu lesen und zu bearbeiten.

strings.context: Notes tab: button on the page of an encrypted note that fetches the key from the system's credential store (Keychain on macOS). Verb, imperative, short.
Notes tab: the unlock button on macOS. The system asks for Touch ID, or for the Mac password when there is no Touch ID; then the key is fetched from the Keychain. Imperative, short.

Notes tab: the unlock button on Windows. The system asks for Windows Hello (face, fingerprint or PIN); then the key is fetched from the Credential Manager. 'Windows Hello' is the product name. Imperative, short.
Notes tab: the line the system's Touch ID or Windows Hello prompt shows while it asks the person to unlock the encrypted notes. Starts after the app name on macOS, so no capital and no full stop.

Notes tab: the line the system's Touch ID or Windows Hello prompt shows while it asks the person before the recovery key of the encrypted notes is shown. Starts after the app name on macOS, so no capital and no full stop.
strings.en: show the recovery key of your encrypted notes
strings.de: den Wiederherstellungsschlüssel deiner verschlüsselten Notizen anzuzeigen

strings.context: Notes tab: line on the page of an encrypted note after the person closed the Touch ID or Windows Hello prompt. The note stays locked.
strings.en: Not unlocked: the prompt was cancelled. The note stays locked.
strings.de: Nicht entsperrt: Die Abfrage wurde abgebrochen. Die Notiz bleibt gesperrt.

strings.context: Notes tab: line on the page of an encrypted note when Touch ID or Windows Hello did not verify the person. {reason} is the system's own text. The note stays locked.
strings.en: Not unlocked: {reason} The note stays locked.
strings.de: Nicht entsperrt: {reason} Die Notiz bleibt gesperrt.

strings.context: Notes tab: notice when a new note was asked for in an encrypted folder but the key is not in memory yet. The key is fetched; the person asks for the note again.
strings.en: That folder is encrypted. Unlocking it now; then make the note again.
strings.de: Dieser Ordner ist verschlüsselt. Er wird jetzt entsperrt, danach legst du die Notiz noch einmal an.

strings.context: Notes tab: error when the system's credential store holds no key for the encrypted notes, for example on a new computer. The recovery key can be entered in the settings.
strings.en: No key for encrypted notes is stored on this computer. Enter the recovery key under Settings > Notes.
strings.de: Auf diesem Computer ist kein Schlüssel für verschlüsselte Notizen gespeichert. Gib den Wiederherstellungsschlüssel unter Einstellungen > Notizen ein.

strings.context: Notes tab: error when the key of the encrypted notes could not be fetched, stored or read. {reason} is the system's own text.
strings.en: The key for encrypted notes is not available: {reason}
strings.de: Der Schlüssel für verschlüsselte Notizen ist nicht verfügbar: {reason}

strings.context: Notes tab: notice when decrypting was asked for while the key is not in memory. The key is fetched; the person asks again.
strings.de: Wird zuerst entsperrt, danach entschlüsselst du noch einmal.

strings.context: Notes tab: notice after a recovery key was accepted and stored on this computer; encrypted notes can be read now.
strings.en: Recovery key accepted. Encrypted notes are unlocked.
strings.de: Wiederherstellungsschlüssel angenommen. Verschlüsselte Notizen sind entsperrt.

strings.context: Notes tab: error when a sync was asked for but no sync folder is set in the settings.
strings.en: No sync folder is set. Choose one under Settings > Notes.
strings.de: Es ist kein Sync-Ordner festgelegt. Wähle einen unter Einstellungen > Notizen.

strings.context: Notes tab: error when copying the notes to the sync folder failed. {reason} is the system's own text.
strings.de: Das Synchronisieren der Notizen ist fehlgeschlagen: {reason}

strings.context: Status bar of the file panels: the note that belongs to the file under the cursor. {line} is the first line of the note, cut short.
Heading of a block on the programs page of the settings: one row per file type that says what F3 does with it. Upper case in German as the other block headings.
Explanation under the heading of the F3-by-file-type block. 'Internal' is the viewer tab of ncrs.
strings.en: The first matching row wins. "Internal" shows the file in a tab of ncrs: Markdown rendered, other text as text.
strings.de: Die erste passende Zeile gilt. „Intern“ zeigt die Datei in einem Tab von ncrs: Markdown gerendert, andere Texte als Text.

strings.context: Label of the field in a file type row where the file name endings are typed, separated by commas, for example md, markdown.
Placeholder in the extensions field of a file type row; the words are examples of file name endings.
Segment of the 'open with' choice: the viewer tab of ncrs itself.
Segment of the 'open with' choice: the program the operating system has for the file.
Segment of the 'open with' choice: a program the user names, as in the viewer and editor settings.
Hint in the place of the program field of a file type row that opens internally: no program is needed.
strings.en: Not needed: ncrs shows the file itself.
strings.de: Nicht nötig: ncrs zeigt die Datei selbst.

strings.context: Hint in the place of the program field of a file type row that opens with the system: no program is needed.
Button next to the program field of a file type row that opens a file dialog to pick the program. Verb, imperative, with an ellipsis because a dialog follows.
Button that deletes a file type row of the F3-by-file-type block. Verb, imperative.
Button that adds an empty file type row to the F3-by-file-type block. Verb, imperative.
Shown under a file type row whose extensions field has no extension, so the row is not saved.
Shown under a file type row that opens with an own program but has no program yet, so the row is not saved.
strings.en: Type the program or choose another way to open.
strings.de: Das Programm eingeben oder eine andere Art zu öffnen wählen.

strings.context: Title of the question before Hermes processes many files in the sources again. {count} is the number of files, always more than one.
Line under the question before Hermes processes many files in the sources again: it explains that Hermes may move them.
strings.en: Hermes reads them again and may move them out of the source.
strings.de: Hermes liest sie neu und verschiebt sie womöglich aus der Quelle.

strings.context: Button that confirms processing the files again. Verb, imperative.
Button that cancels processing the files again. Verb, imperative.
Filing tab: a file Hermes is looking at right now. Starts with a half circle as the mark of the state.
Filing tab: appended to the state of a file the user changed by hand. Starts with a space.
Filing tab: checkbox label over the target tree. On shows only the folders that get new files.
Filing page of the settings, sentence under the page title: what the page is for. Sources are folders files come from, targets are folders they go into, rules say which file goes where.
strings.en: Files from sources go into targets by rules. If no rule matches, the file stays where it is.
strings.de: Dateien aus Quellen kommen nach Regeln in Ziele. Passt keine Regel, bleibt die Datei liegen.

strings.context: Filing page of the settings: heading of the list of source folders, the folders new files are taken from. Noun, plural.
Filing page of the settings: short note after the heading Sources. Says that Hermes watches the folders and files what arrives.
Filing page of the settings: button that opens the dialog for a new source folder. The plus is part of the label; the ellipsis means a dialog follows.
Filing page of the settings: heading of the list of target folders with the rules of each. Targets are the folders files are filed into.
Filing page of the settings: short note after the heading Targets and their rules. The rules of a target are checked in the order of the list.
strings.en: top to bottom, the first match applies
strings.de: von oben nach unten, die erste passende gilt

strings.context: Title of the dialog in which a new target folder is made.
Title of the dialog in which the name and folder of a target are changed.
Label of the name field in the target dialog. The name is optional: the folder's name is shown without one.
Error under the folder field of the target dialog: the folder lies in another target, or another target lies in it. {name} is the name of that other target.
strings.de: Der Ordner überschneidet sich mit dem Ziel {name}.

strings.context: Title of the question before the folder of a target is confirmed as the right one, when none of its known documents is there.
Question before the folder of a target is confirmed as the right one. {count} is the number of documents the index knows in this folder; none of them is there, so the drive may not be connected.
strings.en: Of {count} known documents none is here. Is the drive connected?
strings.de: Von {count} bekannten Dokumenten liegt hier keins. Ist das Laufwerk angeschlossen?

strings.context: Button of the question before the folder of a target is confirmed although none of its known documents is there.
Title of the question before a target is removed.
Question before a target with rules is removed. {name} is the target, {count} the number of its rules, which are deleted with it. The files in the folder stay.
strings.en: Remove the target {name} with its {count} rules? The rules are deleted, the files in the folder stay. Sources lose this target; a source left without a target pauses.
strings.de: Ziel {name} mit seinen {count} Regeln entfernen? Die Regeln werden gelöscht, die Dateien im Ordner bleiben. Quellen verlieren dieses Ziel; eine Quelle ohne Ziel pausiert.

strings.context: Question before a target without rules is removed. {name} is the target. The files in the folder stay.
strings.en: Remove the target {name}? The files in the folder stay. Sources lose this target; a source left without a target pauses.
strings.de: Ziel {name} entfernen? Die Dateien im Ordner bleiben. Quellen verlieren dieses Ziel; eine Quelle ohne Ziel pausiert.

strings.context: Error under the pattern field of the rule dialog: {block} is a word in braces the pattern does not know. The blocks to use are the chips under the field.
strings.en: {block} is not a block of the pattern. Use the blocks below the field.
strings.de: {block} ist kein Baustein des Musters. Nimm die Bausteine unter dem Feld.
