strings.context: Line of the trial run in the rule dialog: the rule fits a file but another file would already have the place. {path} is the place.
strings.en: {path} · name already taken · stays where it is

strings.context: Line of the trial run in the rule dialog: the rule fits a file but the pattern gives a name that not every system keeps.
strings.en: not a valid file name · stays where it is

strings.context: Line of the trial run in the rule dialog: {count} files of the sources have no text, so no rule can decide about them; they are asked about.
Filing page of the settings: button that opens the dialog for a new target folder. The plus is part of the label; the ellipsis means a dialog follows.
Filing page of the settings: button on the line of a target that opens the dialog for a new rule of this target. The plus is part of the label.
Filing page of the settings: button on the line of a target that already has rules. Hermes reads the folders of the target that no rule covers and proposes rules for them.
Filing page of the settings: main button on the line of a target that has no rules yet. Hermes reads the target and the sources and proposes a whole set of rules, the scheme.
Filing page of the settings: warning on the line of a target that has no rules yet. A scheme is the set of rules that says which file goes into which folder.
Filing page of the settings: second line of a target. {path} is the folder of the target, {sources} the names of the sources whose files can come into it, separated by commas.
Filing page of the settings: second line of a target that no source files into. {path} is the folder of the target.
Filing page of the settings: status on the line of a source. {files} is what happens to the files (move or copy), {no_text} what happens to a file in which no text was found (ask or skip).
Filing page of the settings: part of the status of a source, the files are moved into the target. Lower case verb, fills {files} of the status.
Filing page of the settings: part of the status of a source, the files are copied into the target. Lower case verb, fills {files} of the status.
Filing page of the settings: part of the status of a source, a file without recognised text makes Hermes ask what to do. Lower case, fills {no_text} of the status.
Filing page of the settings: part of the status of a source, a file without recognised text is skipped and stays where it is. Lower case, fills {no_text} of the status.
Filing page of the settings: button on the line of a source, a target or a rule that opens its dialog. Verb.
Filing page of the settings: button on the line of a source or a target, and in the dialog of a rule, that removes it. Files already filed stay where they are. Verb.
Button on a source of the sorting page whose folder cannot be read (moved, drive missing, no permission): the user chooses the folder again, everything else of the source stays.
Filing page of the settings: shown under the heading Sources while the list is empty.
Filing page of the settings: shown under the heading Targets and their rules while the list is empty.
Source dialog: hint while there is no target to choose, so the source cannot be saved yet. A button next to it makes a target.
Title of the dialog of a source folder that Hermes watches. Noun.
Title of the dialog that files the files of one folder once, opened from the context menu of a folder. The same dialog as for a source, without watching.
Source dialog: label of the field with the path of the folder the files are taken from.
Source dialog: label of the field with the file patterns to take. Several patterns are separated by a semicolon, an empty field takes every file.
Source dialog: grey example in the empty Include field. Two file patterns separated by a semicolon; the same in every language.
Source dialog: label of the field with the file patterns to leave out. Several patterns are separated by a semicolon.
Source dialog: label of the list of targets with a tick box each. The files of the source may go into the ticked targets.
Source dialog: label of the choice between watching the folder all the time and filing it once.
Source dialog: choice of the field When. Hermes watches the folder and files what arrives. Verb.
Source dialog: choice of the field When. The folder is filed one time, nothing is watched afterwards.
Source dialog: label of the choice between copying and moving the files into the target.
Source dialog: choice of the field Files. The original stays in the source. Verb.
Source dialog: choice of the field Files. The original leaves the source. Verb.
Source dialog: label of the choice what happens to a file in which no text was recognised.
Source dialog: choice of the field No text found. Hermes asks what to do with the file. Verb.
Source dialog: choice of the field No text found. The file is skipped and stays where it is. Verb.
Source dialog: label of the choice what happens to a file that matches rules of several targets.
Source dialog: choice of the field Several targets match. Hermes asks which targets get the file. Verb.
Source dialog: choice of the field Several targets match. The file is copied into every target that matches.
Button of the dialog that files a folder once: closes the dialog and shows the plan of what would happen, nothing is moved yet.
Source dialog: error under the Include or Exclude field. {pattern} is the file pattern that cannot be used, as the user typed it.
Source dialog: error under the Folder field when the folder does not exist.
Source dialog: error under the list of targets when none is ticked. A source without a target is paused.
Source dialog: error under the Folder field when a watched folder lies in a target folder (or is one): filed files would be filed again.
strings.en: A watched folder cannot be inside a target.
strings.de: Ein überwachter Ordner darf nicht in einem Ziel liegen.

strings.context: Source dialog: warning under the choice Watch, when a target or a folder of the index lies inside the chosen folder. New files in the folder are then not read and filed by themselves, only with the plan.
strings.en: A target or a folder of the index lies inside this folder: new files are not filed by themselves, they appear in the plan.
strings.de: In diesem Ordner liegt ein Ziel oder ein Ordner des Index: Neue Dateien werden nicht von selbst einsortiert, sie erscheinen im Plan.

strings.context: Source dialog: hint under the choice Watch. Files that are in the folder already are not filed by themselves; they show up in the plan.
strings.en: Files that are in the folder already stay; they appear in the plan.
strings.de: Was schon im Ordner liegt, bleibt liegen und erscheint im Plan.

strings.context: Filing page of the settings: state on the line of a source that has no target and so does nothing.
Filing page of the settings: state on the line of a source whose drive is not plugged in. The source waits.
Filing page of the settings: state on the line of a source whose folder does not exist. The source waits.
Filing page of the settings: state on the line of a source whose folder cannot be read, for example without the permission of the system.
Filing page of the settings: state on the line of a source when a target it files into is not ready, for example its drive is missing.
Filing page of the settings: state on the line of a source whose include or exclude pattern cannot be used.
Filing page of the settings: state on the line of a source with exactly one open question about a file.
Filing page of the settings: state on the line of a source with open questions about files, for none or more than one. {count} is the number.
Filing page of the settings: title of the group that lists the last runs with the button to take one back. Noun.
Rule dialog: label of the dropdown that chooses the target folder the files of this rule are filed into.
Filing page: state on the line of a target taken over from an older version, whose folder was never confirmed as the right one. The button Confirm sits next to it.
Filing page: button on the line of a target whose folder was never confirmed; confirms that the folder is the right one.
Rule dialog: heading in capitals over the pattern, after the conditions. Reads “if the document … then into …”.
Rule dialog: label of the field with the pattern that makes the path and the name of the filed file, built from blocks like the sender and the date.
Rule dialog: dimmed line under the pattern. {path} is the full path a real example document would get.
Rule dialog, trial run: a document has no recognised date, so the block {block} of the pattern stays empty and the file is left where it is. {block} is the block in braces, e.g. the year.
strings.en: no date found, {block} stays empty · stays where it is
strings.de: kein Datum erkannt, {block} bleibt leer · bleibt liegen

strings.context: Rule dialog, trial run: no text was recognised in a document and Hermes will ask what to do with it.
Filing tab: heading over the left list, before the folder of the source and its file patterns. Noun.
Filing tab: heading over the right tree, before the chips of the targets. Noun, plural.
Filing tab: column heading of the left list. Shows which rule matches a file and where it goes.
Filing tab: what happens to a file. {rule} is the name of the matching rule, {target} the short name of the target (T1), {path} the new path of the file inside the target.
Filing tab: the file is in the target already. {target} is the short name of the target (T1), {path} the path of the existing file inside it.
Filing tab: no rule matches the file, so it is not filed. Links to make a rule follow.
strings.en: no rule matches · stays where it is

strings.context: Filing tab: no text was recognised in the file, so no rule can match. A link to ask follows.
strings.en: no text found · stays where it is

strings.context: Filing tab: rules of several targets match the file. {targets} is the list of their short names, e.g. “T1 and T2”.
Two short names of targets joined, e.g. “T1 and T2”. {first} and {second} are the names.
Filing tab: link behind a file that no rule matches. Opens the rule dialog filled with what is known of the file. The ellipsis means a dialog follows.
Filing tab: link behind a file that no rule matches. Hermes proposes the missing rule.
Filing tab: link behind a file that cannot be filed without a decision of the user (no text, several targets). Opens the question. Lower case verb.
Filing tab, status bar: how many files of the source were looked at. {count} is the number.
Filing tab, status bar: how many files a rule puts into a target. {count} is the number.
Filing tab, status bar: how many files are in their target already. {count} is the number.
Filing tab, status bar: how many files no rule matches. {count} is the number.
Filing tab, status bar: how many files have no recognised text. {count} is the number.
Filing tab, status bar: how many files match rules of several targets. {count} is the number, {targets} the short names of those targets.
Filing tab, button in the status bar: copies the files that a rule files. {count} is the number of files.
Filing tab, button in the status bar: moves the files that a rule files. {count} is the number of files.
Filing tab, subtitle of the question about one file: rules of two targets match it.
Filing tab, line of the question about one file, behind the chip of a target. {rule} is the name of the rule, {path} the path the file would get.
Filing tab, button of the question about one file that matches two targets: copy it into both.
Filing tab, button of the question about one file that matches two targets: file it into one only. {target} is its short name (T1).
Filing tab, hint beside the Esc key in the question about one file: the file is left where it is.
Title of the dialog in which Hermes proposes a whole set of rules for a target that has none.
Scheme dialog: what Hermes looked at. {files} is the number of files read, {sources} the number of sources, {fit} how many files the proposed {rules} rules match, {rest} how many no rule matches.
strings.en: Read: {files} files in {sources} sources. {fit} match these {rules} rules, {rest} match none.
strings.de: Gelesen: {files} Dateien in {sources} Quellen. Davon passen {fit} in diese {rules} Regeln, {rest} in keine.

strings.context: Button of the dialogs in which Hermes proposes rules: asks for a different proposal.
Main button of the dialogs in which Hermes proposes rules when one rule is ticked: saves it. Pairs with sorting.take_rules.
Main button of the dialogs in which Hermes proposes rules: saves the ticked rules. {count} is the number of rules.
Scheme dialog: dimmed line under the pattern of a proposed rule. {example} is the path a real file would get.
Scheme dialog and rule proposals: how many files a proposed rule matches. {count} is the number.
Title of the dialog in which Hermes proposes the one rule that a file without a matching rule needs.
Rule proposal dialog: what Hermes recognised in the file. {facts} lists sender, kind and date.
Rule proposal dialog: heading in capitals over the fields of the new rule. {target} is the chip text and name of the target the rule goes into.
Rule proposal dialog: label of the line with the condition of the new rule. Reads “if: sender is …”.
Rule proposal dialog: the new rule also matches other files that lie in the source. {count} is the number of those files.
Rule proposal dialog: button that opens the full rule dialog with the proposal. The ellipsis means a dialog follows.
Rule proposal dialog: main button that saves the proposed rule.
Title of the dialog in which Hermes proposes more rules for a target that has rules already.
Rules proposal dialog: what is missing. {rules} is the number of rules the target has, {folders} the number of folders of the target that no rule covers.
strings.en: {rules} rules exist. {folders} folders in the target are covered by no rule:
strings.de: {rules} Regeln sind da. {folders} Ordner im Ziel deckt keine Regel ab:

strings.context: Rules proposal dialog: line shown when the model found nothing to propose.
strings.en: Hermes found no further rule to suggest.
strings.de: Hermes hat keine weitere Regel gefunden.

strings.context: Dialogs in which Hermes proposes rules: line shown while Hermes reads the files and the model works. It can take a while.
strings.en: Hermes is reading the files and writing proposals…
strings.de: Hermes liest die Dateien und schreibt Vorschläge …

strings.context: Dialogs in which Hermes proposes rules: error line when no proposal could be made. {detail} is the technical reason.
strings.en: Hermes could not make a proposal: {detail}

strings.context: Dialogs in which Hermes proposes rules: grey note when Hermes is switched off or has no model. The proposals then come from the folders and files alone.
strings.en: No model is available, so the proposals come from the folders and files alone.
strings.de: Kein Modell verfügbar, die Vorschläge kommen allein aus Ordnern und Dateien.

strings.context: Dialogs in which Hermes proposes rules: grey note when the model did not answer. {detail} is the technical reason. The proposals then come from the folders and files alone.
strings.en: The model did not answer ({detail}), so the proposals come from the folders and files alone.
strings.de: Das Modell hat nicht geantwortet ({detail}), die Vorschläge kommen allein aus Ordnern und Dateien.

strings.context: Rule proposal dialog for one file: line shown when no rule could be found that fits the file.
strings.en: Hermes found no rule that fits this file.
strings.de: Hermes hat keine Regel gefunden, die zu dieser Datei passt.

strings.context: Dialogs in which Hermes proposes rules: button on one proposed rule. It turns the proposal down for good, so Hermes does not propose it again for this target.
Filing tab: line under the existing files of a folder of the target, grey. {count} is how many more files are there that are not listed.
Filing tab: checkbox label in the bar. When on, the files of the source that are already in a target are moved to the trash.
strings.en: Move duplicates in the source to the trash
strings.de: Duplikate aus der Quelle in den Papierkorb

strings.context: Filing tab: error line when the user picked a folder that is not inside a target of the source.
strings.en: The folder is not inside a target of this source.
strings.de: Der Ordner liegt in keinem Ziel dieser Quelle.

strings.context: Filing tab: error line when a new file name is empty, has a slash in it, or is only one or two dots.
strings.en: A file name must not be empty, contain a slash or be only dots.
strings.de: Ein Dateiname darf nicht leer sein, keinen Schrägstrich enthalten und nicht nur aus Punkten bestehen.

strings.context: Filing tab: placeholder of the field in which the new name of a file is typed.
Filing tab: line in the left list when the source has no files to file.
strings.en: No files to file in this folder.
strings.de: In diesem Ordner gibt es keine Dateien zum Einsortieren.

strings.context: Filing tab: title of the tab. {folder} is the name of the source folder.
Filing tab: what happens to a file whose new name is taken by another file, in the target or in the plan. {target} is the short name of the target (T1), {path} the path that is taken.
strings.en: name taken: {target} {path} · stays where it is

strings.context: Filing tab: the pattern of the rule needs a value that was not found in the file, so it is not filed. {field} is the name of the value (Sender, Number), {block} the part of the pattern it belongs to, like {number}.
strings.en: {field} not found, {block} stays empty · stays where it is
strings.de: {field} nicht erkannt, {block} bleibt leer · bleibt liegen

strings.context: Filing tab: the pattern of a rule gives no usable file name for the file, so it is not filed. {rule} is the name of the rule.
strings.en: rule {rule} gives no usable name · stays where it is
strings.de: Regel {rule} ergibt keinen brauchbaren Namen · bleibt liegen

strings.context: Filing tab: the file could not be read, so no rule can match. {reason} says why, see the reasons that follow.
strings.en: not read: {reason} · stays where it is

strings.context: Filing tab: reason a file was not read. Follows 'not read:'. Short, no full stop.
Filing tab: reason a file was not read. Follows 'not read:'. Another program is still writing the file. Short, no full stop.
Filing tab: reason a file was not read. Follows 'not read:'. Short, no full stop.
strings.en: no text can be read from this kind of file
strings.de: aus dieser Dateiart lässt sich kein Text lesen

strings.context: Filing tab: reason a file was not read. Follows 'not read:'. The library that reads PDF files is missing. Short, no full stop.
Filing tab: a file of a watched source that the user left or whose filing was taken back; it is not decided for again.
strings.en: set aside · stays where it is

strings.context: Colored field at the left end of the bar of the filing tab. Upper case, a single short word.
Filing tab of a watched source: no rule matches the file. Three links follow in the same row, so as short as possible.
Filing tab: the user chose to leave this file where it is.
Filing tab: link behind a file that has no place yet. Opens the choice of a target folder for this one file. The ellipsis means a choice follows.
Filing tab: link behind a file that waits for a decision. The file stays where it is. Lower case verb phrase.
Filing tab: why a target cannot be filed into. Follows the name of the target. Short, no full stop.
Filing tab: why a target cannot be filed into. Follows the name of the target. The drive of the target is not connected. Short, no full stop.
Filing tab: why a target cannot be filed into. Follows the name of the target. Short, no full stop.
Filing tab: why a target cannot be filed into. Follows the name of the target. The folder was taken over from an older version and none of its files is there. Short, no full stop.
Filing tab: why a target cannot be filed into. Follows the name of the target. The user paused it. Short, no full stop.
Filing tab: line above the bar while a target cannot be filed into; nothing is filed until it can. {target} is the short name of the target (T1), {reason} why it cannot.
strings.en: {target} is waiting: {reason}. Nothing is filed until then.
strings.de: {target} wartet: {reason}. Bis dahin wird nichts einsortiert.

strings.context: Filing tab: button that looks at the source and the targets again after the user fixed something, for example connected a drive.
Filing tab, status bar: how many files have a problem the user has to look at (name taken, no usable name, no value for the pattern, not read). {count} is the number.
Filing tab, status bar: how many files of the source were read while the plan is made. {done} is the number read so far, {total} all files.
Filing tab, status bar: figure while the files are being carried out. {done} is the number finished so far, {total} all files.
Filing tab, status bar: result of a run. {count} is the number of files that reached their place.
Filing tab, status bar: result of a run. {count} is the number of files that are still in the source.
Filing tab, status bar: result of a run. {count} is the number of duplicates in the source that went to the trash.
Filing tab: error line for one file that was not filed because its target cannot be filed into. {file} is the file name, {reason} why the target cannot.
Filing tab: error line for one file that was not filed because its place is not usable (not a target of the source, or a name that does not work on every system). {file} is the file name.
Filing tab: error line for one file that was not filed because it changed or went away after the plan was made. {file} is the file name.
strings.en: {file}: changed or gone since the plan was made.
strings.de: {file}: seit dem Plan geändert oder nicht mehr da.

strings.context: Filing tab: error line for one file that was not filed because another file has its name in the target. {file} is the file name.
strings.en: {file}: the name is taken in the target.
strings.de: {file}: der Name ist im Ziel vergeben.

strings.context: Filing tab: error line for one file that was not filed because the run was stopped before. {file} is the file name.
Filing tab: error line for one file that could not be filed. {file} is the file name, {reason} what the system said.
Filing tab: error line after the first files that were not filed. {count} is how many more there are.
Filing tab: error line when the folder of the source cannot be read, for example because its drive is not connected.
strings.en: The source folder cannot be read. Check the folder and try again.
strings.de: Der Quellordner kann nicht gelesen werden. Prüfe den Ordner und versuche es noch einmal.

strings.context: Filing tab, subtitle of the question about one file that matches more than two targets. {count} is the number of targets.
Filing tab, button of the question about one file that matches more than two targets: copy it into every target.
Filing tab, button of the question about one file that matches more than two targets: file it into the ticked targets.
Reason in an error line: the file or folder is not there (any more). Short, no full stop; it is put into a sentence like 'Comparison stopped: {reason}'.
Reason in an error line: the system refuses access to the file or folder. Short, no full stop.
Reason in an error line: a file or folder of that name is already there. Short, no full stop.
Reason in an error line: the disk has no space left. Short, no full stop.
Reason in an error line: the disk or folder cannot be written to, it is read-only. Short, no full stop.
Reason in an error line: the disk or server did not answer in time. Short, no full stop.
strings.de: keine Antwort in der erwarteten Zeit

strings.context: Reason in an error line: a folder cannot be removed because it still holds something. Short, no full stop.
Reason in an error line: the operation cannot be done between two different disks. Short, no full stop.
strings.en: cannot be done between two disks

strings.context: Reason in an error line: the user's storage quota on the disk or server is used up. Short, no full stop.
strings.en: the storage quota is used up

strings.context: Status or error line when something needs the document index but it is not open (Hermes is off or still starting). Calm, one short sentence.

Plural noun in the list of what an unpacking left out: files whose name another file of the archive had already taken, for example two names that differ only in capital letters on a disk that does not tell them apart. Lower case, used inside a comma-separated list.
Notice when a file that was asked to be read again was not read, because Hermes was rebuilt or restarted meanwhile and forgot the request. Takes the file name; the user can ask again.
strings.en: {name}: could not be read again, Hermes was restarted. Ask again.
strings.de: {name}: konnte nicht erneut gelesen werden, Hermes wurde neu gestartet. Frag noch einmal.

strings.context: Status bar error when Hermes could not read its information about files from the index (for the Hermes column or for processing a file again). {reason} is the technical cause.
strings.en: Hermes could not read the index: {reason}
strings.de: Hermes konnte den Index nicht lesen: {reason}

strings.context: Status bar error shown when Hermes opened its index but could not finish the filing steps that an earlier run left half done. They stay pending and are tried again at the next start. {reason} is the technical cause.
strings.en: Hermes could not finish earlier filing steps, they are tried again at the next start: {reason}
strings.de: Hermes konnte frühere Ablageschritte nicht abschließen, sie werden beim nächsten Start erneut versucht: {reason}

strings.context: Batch rename dialog. Dimmed line under the new-name pattern field. The words inside the curly braces (name, counter, date modified, date taken, extension, sender, document date, kind, amount) are the same in every language and must stay in English, as the pattern is typed that way. Keep the braces and the words inside them untouched.
strings.en: Parts in braces are written the same in every language, e.g. {name}, {counter}, {date modified}. The buttons below insert them.
strings.de: Teile in geschweiften Klammern werden in jeder Sprache gleich geschrieben, z. B. {name}, {counter}, {date modified}. Die Knöpfe unten fügen sie ein.

strings.context: Shown under the name input of a row being renamed, in the batch rename preview and in the prompt for a new folder or file when the name is longer than the file system takes (255 bytes, on Windows 255 characters).
strings.en: The name is too long, a file system takes at most 255 characters
strings.de: Der Name ist zu lang, ein Dateisystem nimmt höchstens 255 Zeichen

strings.context: Shown on Windows when a typed name is one Windows opens as a device (CON, PRN, AUX, NUL, COM1 to COM9, LPT1 to LPT9), with or without an ending. Keep the device names in capitals.
strings.en: Windows reserves this name (CON, NUL, COM1 and similar)
strings.de: Windows hat diesen Namen reserviert (CON, NUL, COM1 und ähnliche)

strings.context: Shown in the prompt for a new folder or file on Windows when the name holds one of the characters < > : " | ? * which Windows does not allow in names. The character is not named here.
strings.de: Ein Name darf keines der Zeichen < > : " | ? * enthalten

strings.context: Status bar notice when a permissions change could not be applied to one entry. {name} is its name, {reason} the system's reason, which stays untranslated.
Status bar notice after a permissions change that changed exactly one entry. {count} is 1.
Shown when the copy that F3 opens for viewing could not be made, for an entry inside an archive or on a server. Takes the entry's name and the system's reason, which stays untranslated.
strings.de: {name} konnte zum Ansehen nicht entpackt werden: {reason}

strings.context: Shown below the empty process table on the Monitor page when the filter field has text and no process matches it. {filter} is the text typed into the filter.
Error when F3 meets something that is not an ordinary file, such as a named pipe or a device. {name} is the file name.
strings.en: {name} is not an ordinary file and is not shown.
strings.de: {name} ist keine normale Datei und wird nicht angezeigt.

strings.context: Entry of the command list and of the folder context menu that opens the Git tab for the repository the cursor or the folder is in. Only offered inside a Git repository. Verb phrase, imperative.
Status line when the Git view is asked for in a folder that is not inside a Git repository.
strings.en: This folder is not inside a Git repository.
strings.de: Dieser Ordner liegt in keinem Git-Repository.

strings.context: Status line when the history or the blame of a file is asked for while the cursor is not on a file inside a Git repository.
strings.en: The cursor is not on a file inside a Git repository.
strings.de: Der Cursor steht auf keiner Datei in einem Git-Repository.

strings.context: Title of the Git tab. {repo} is the name of the repository folder. Git is the product name and stays as it is.
Mode field at the left of the status bar of the Git tab. Product name, stays as it is.
Git tab: what a list or the right side says while the repository is being read.
Git tab: what the commit list says when the repository has no commits or the filter matches none.
Git tab: button below the commit list that reads the next commits. Verb, imperative.
Git tab: shown in the status line when the repository cannot be read. {reason} is the reason Git gives.
Git tab: placeholder of the filter field in the header; it filters the commit list by message, author or the start of the commit hash (SHA).
Git tab: heading of the group of local branches in the left list. Upper case, short.

Git tab: heading of the group of remotes in the left list. Below it each remote (a server copy of the repository, such as origin) is one line with its branches under it, the number of remote branches is added in brackets. Upper case, short.
Git tab: heading of the group of tags in the left list. Upper case, short. Tags are named marks on commits, like releases.
Git tab: heading of the group of stashes in the left list, the number of shelved changes is added in brackets. Upper case, short.
Git tab: heading of the group of worktrees in the left list. A worktree is a second folder of the same repository with its own branch checked out. Upper case, short.
Git tab: part of a worktree line that says the worktree has unsaved changes (work in progress). {count} is the number of changed files. Keep it very short.
Git tab: part of a worktree line that says everything on its branch is already in the main branch, so the worktree can go. One word.
Git tab: shown in the header instead of the branch name when no branch is checked out. {sha} is the first characters of the commit.
Git tab: header of the column with the commit messages. Upper case, short.
Git tab: header of the column with the authors of the commits. Upper case, short.
Git tab: header of the column with the dates of the commits. Upper case, short.
Git tab: header of the column with the short commit hashes. SHA is the name of the hash and stays as it is.
Git tab: what the right side says while no commit is chosen.
Git tab: segment that lists the changed files of a commit with their full paths. Noun, short.
Git tab: segment that lists the changed files of a commit as a tree of folders. Noun, short.
Git tab: segment that shows the diff with the old file on the left and the new file on the right. Short.
Git tab: segment that shows the diff as one column with removed and added lines one above the other. Short.
Git tab: checkbox of the diff; when on, lines that differ only in spaces and tabs count as equal.
Git tab: what the diff says while the two versions of the file are being compared.
Git tab: what the diff says for a file that is not text (an image, an archive).
strings.en: Binary file, no text to compare.

strings.context: Git tab: what the diff says for a text file that is too large to compare line by line.
strings.en: The file is too large to compare.
strings.de: Die Datei ist zu groß zum Vergleichen.

strings.context: Git tab: what a comparison of two commits, or of a commit with the working copy, says when they do not differ in any file.
strings.en: These two versions do not differ.
strings.de: Diese beiden Stände unterscheiden sich nicht.

strings.context: Git tab: what the diff says when the two versions of the file do not differ, for example after ignoring whitespace.
Git tab: note at the right end of the status bar. {count} is the number of commits read so far.
Git tab: status line while the left list has the keys. Keep the key names as they are on the keyboard; Tab changes the area, the slash starts the filter.
strings.en: ↑↓ choose · ←→ fold · Enter shows the worktree · Tab next area · / filter · Esc closes
strings.de: ↑↓ wählen · ←→ falten · Enter zeigt den Worktree · Tab nächster Bereich · / Filter · Esc schließt

strings.context: Git tab: status line while the commit list has the keys. Keep the key names as they are on the keyboard.
strings.en: ↑↓ choose · Enter to the files · Tab next area · / filter · Esc closes
strings.de: ↑↓ wählen · Enter zu den Dateien · Tab nächster Bereich · / Filter · Esc schließt

strings.context: Git tab: status line while the file list of a commit has the keys. Keep the key names as they are on the keyboard.
strings.en: ↑↓ choose · Enter opens the diff · Tab next area · / filter · Esc closes
strings.de: ↑↓ wählen · Enter öffnet den Diff · Tab nächster Bereich · / Filter · Esc schließt

strings.context: Git tab: status line while the filter field has the keyboard. Keep the key names as they are on the keyboard.
strings.en: Type to filter · Enter or Esc back to the list
strings.de: Tippen zum Filtern · Enter oder Esc zurück zur Liste

strings.context: Git tab: status line while a diff is shown. The placeholders are keys as the platform spells them. Keep the arrows, the keys n, p and F3 and the key name Esc.
strings.en: ↑↓ scroll · n/p next/previous change · {previous_file}/{next_file} other file · F3 view file · Esc back
strings.de: ↑↓ scrollen · n/p nächste/vorige Änderung · {previous_file}/{next_file} andere Datei · F3 Datei ansehen · Esc zurück

strings.context: Git tab, local changes: heading of the list of changed files that are not staged yet. The number follows in brackets.
Git tab, local changes: heading of the list of files that go into the next commit. The number follows in brackets.
Git tab, local changes: tooltip of the icon button that stages every changed file. Short.
Git tab, local changes: tooltip of the icon button that takes every staged file out of the next commit. Short.
Git tab, local changes: tooltip of the icon button at the end of a file row that stages the file. Short.
Git tab, local changes: tooltip of the icon button at the end of a staged file row that takes it out of the next commit. Short.
Git tab, local changes: tooltip of the icon button of one hunk of a diff that stages only this hunk. Short.
Git tab, local changes: tooltip of the icon button of one hunk of a diff that throws the change of this hunk away for good. Short.
Git tab, local changes: placeholder of the one-line title of the commit message.
Git tab, local changes: label above the longer text of the commit message, which may stay empty.
Git tab, local changes: checkbox that puts the staged files into the last commit instead of a new one. amend is the Git word and stays.
Git tab, local changes: button that commits exactly one staged file.
Git tab, local changes: button that commits the staged files. {count} is the number of staged files, 0 or 2 and more.
Git tab, toolbar: tooltip of the icon button that asks the remote what is new without changing anything. Short.
Git tab, toolbar: tooltip of the icon button that brings the commits of the remote into the branch. Pull is the Git word and stays. Short.
Git tab, toolbar: tooltip of the icon button that sends the local commits to the remote. Push is the Git word and stays. Short.
Git tab, toolbar: tooltip of the icon button that shelves the local changes. Stash is the Git word and stays. Short.
Git tab, toolbar: tooltip of the icon button that takes back the last local action. {what} says what it would take back, for example a commit with its title.
Git tab, context menu of a local branch: switch the folder to this branch.
Git tab, context menu of a branch: opens the dialog that creates a new branch starting here.
Git tab, context menu of a branch: opens the dialog that renames it.
Git tab, context menu: delete the branch or the stash after a question.
Git tab, context menu of a branch: merge this branch into the branch that is checked out. {branch} is the checked-out branch.
Git tab, context menu of a branch: replay the checked-out branch on top of this branch. {branch} is the checked-out branch.
Git tab, context menu of a remote branch: create a local branch that follows it and switch to it.
Git tab, context menu of a remote branch: delete the branch on the server after a question.
Git tab, context menu of a stash: put the shelved changes back and keep the stash.
Git tab, context menu of a stash: put the shelved changes back and delete the stash.
Git tab, dialog title: create a branch.
Git tab, new branch dialog: label of the name field.
Git tab, new branch dialog: placeholder of the name field, an example name.
Git tab, new branch dialog: says where the branch starts. {from} is a branch name or a short commit id with its title.
Git tab, new branch dialog: checkbox that switches to the new branch right away.
Git tab, new branch dialog: the button that creates the branch.
Git tab, new branch dialog: problem shown when the name has a space in it.
strings.en: The name must not contain spaces.
strings.de: Der Name darf keine Leerzeichen enthalten.

strings.context: Git tab, dialogs: button that closes the dialog without doing anything.
Git tab: banner while a merge is stopped by conflicts. {from} is the merged branch, {into} the checked-out branch, {count} the number of files still in conflict.
Git tab: banner while a merge is stopped by exactly one conflict. {from} is the merged branch, {into} the checked-out branch.
Git tab: banner of a merge whose conflicts are all resolved. {from} is the merged branch, {into} the checked-out branch.
strings.en: Merge of {from} into {into}: all conflicts resolved
strings.de: Merge von {from} in {into}: alle Konflikte gelöst

strings.context: Git tab: second line of the merge banner, says what to do.
strings.en: Resolve every file, then continue. Abort puts everything back as it was before the merge.
strings.de: Löse jede Datei, dann fortsetzen. Abbrechen stellt alles wie vor dem Merge wieder her.

strings.context: Git tab: banner while a rebase is stopped by conflicts. {from} is the branch the commits are replayed onto, {into} the checked-out branch being rebased, {count} the number of files still in conflict.
Git tab: banner while a rebase is stopped by exactly one conflict. {from} is the branch the commits are replayed onto, {into} the checked-out branch being rebased.
Git tab: banner of a rebase whose conflicts are all resolved. {from} is the branch the commits are replayed onto, {into} the checked-out branch being rebased.
strings.en: Rebase of {into} onto {from}: all conflicts resolved
strings.de: Rebase von {into} auf {from}: alle Konflikte gelöst

strings.context: Git tab: second line of the rebase banner, says what to do.
strings.en: Resolve every file, then continue. Abort puts everything back as it was before the rebase.
strings.de: Löse jede Datei, dann fortsetzen. Abbrechen stellt alles wie vor dem Rebase wieder her.

strings.context: Git tab: button of the merge banner that cancels the merge. Short.
Git tab: button of the merge banner that finishes the merge. Short.
Git tab, conflict list: tooltip of the icon button that keeps the version of the checked-out branch for the whole file. Short. Also the entry of the conflict menu.
Git tab, conflict list: tooltip of the icon button that keeps the version of the merged branch for the whole file. Short. Also the entry of the conflict menu.
Git tab, conflict list: button that opens the file in the editor to resolve it by hand.
Git tab, conflict list: how many places of a file are in conflict. {count} is 2 or more.
Git tab, conflict list: a file with exactly one place in conflict.
Git tab, conflict list: shown after a file that is resolved.
Git tab, diff of a conflict: line above the lines of the checked-out branch. {branch} is its name.
Git tab, diff of a conflict: line above the lines of the merged branch. {branch} is its name.
Git tab, diff of a conflict: line that ends the conflicting place.
Git tab: button that closes a notice. Short.
Git tab: headline of the notice after a push the remote turned down.
Git tab: explanation of a rejected push. {branch} is the branch, {count} the number of commits on the remote it lacks.
strings.en: The remote has {count} commits on {branch} that you do not have yet. Fetch them with a pull first, then push again.
strings.de: Auf dem Remote liegen {count} Commits auf {branch}, die du noch nicht hast. Hol sie zuerst mit einem Pull, dann pushe noch einmal.

strings.context: Git tab: button of the rejected push notice that does a pull. Short.
Git tab: headline of the notice when the remote does not let the user in. {remote} is the name of the remote.
Git tab: explanation of a failed login to a remote.
strings.en: The server turned down the login. Check your SSH key or the saved password, then try again.
strings.de: Der Server hat die Anmeldung abgelehnt. Prüfe deinen SSH-Schlüssel oder das gespeicherte Passwort und versuche es noch einmal.

strings.context: Git tab: button of the failed login notice that tries the push or pull again. Short.
Git tab, local changes: tooltip of the icon button of a not staged file that throws its changes away for good after a question. Short, the dots say a question follows.
Git tab, local changes: tooltip of the icon button that throws all not staged changes away for good after a question. Short.
Git tab, local changes: tooltip of the icon button of one hunk of a staged file that takes only this hunk out of the next commit. Short.
Git tab, conflict list: tooltip of the icon button that keeps both versions of the file, mine first. Short. Also the entry of the conflict menu.
Git tab, conflict list: button of a file that was edited by hand, says the file is fine now. Short.
Git tab, conflict list: button of a resolved file that brings the conflict back. Short.
Git tab, conflict list: shown after a file that was changed in the editor but is not marked as resolved yet.
Git tab, context menu of a local branch that has commits the remote lacks: send them. Short.
Git tab: button of a notice that shows the message git printed. Short.

Git tab: status line while the left list has the keys and the actions are on. {menu} opens the menu of the row, {new_branch} starts a new branch; both are keys as the platform spells them. Keep the other key names as they are on the keyboard.
strings.en: ↑↓ choose · ←→ fold · Enter shows the worktree · {menu} actions · {new_branch} new branch · Tab next area · Esc closes
strings.de: ↑↓ wählen · ←→ falten · Enter zeigt den Worktree · {menu} Aktionen · {new_branch} Neuer Branch · Tab nächster Bereich · Esc schließt

strings.context: Git tab: status line while a merge with conflicts is shown. The placeholders are keys as the platform spells them. Keep the other key names.
strings.en: ↑↓ choose file · {mine} mine · {theirs} theirs · {both} both · {editor} editor · {resolved} resolved · {menu} actions
strings.de: ↑↓ Datei wählen · {mine} meine · {theirs} ihre · {both} beide · {editor} Editor · {resolved} gelöst · {menu} Aktionen

strings.context: Git tab: quiet line under the header when the actions are off because git is not installed. git is the name of the program and stays lowercase.
strings.en: Git actions need git to be installed

strings.context: Git tab: quiet line under the header in the App Store version, which runs no git actions. Homebrew is the name of a package manager and stays.
strings.en: Git actions are only in the Homebrew version
strings.de: Git-Aktionen gibt es in der Homebrew-Version

strings.context: Git tab: the name of a stash made with the stash button, which asks for none. {branch} is the branch that is checked out.
Git tab, toolbar: what the undo button would take back, shown after "Undo: ". One file was staged (put into the next commit). Lowercase, no full stop.
Git tab, toolbar: what the undo button would take back, shown after "Undo: ". {count} files were staged (put into the next commit). Lowercase, no full stop.
Git tab, toolbar: what the undo button would take back, shown after "Undo: ". All changes were staged at once. Lowercase, no full stop.
Git tab, toolbar: what the undo button would take back, shown after "Undo: ". One file was taken out of the next commit again. Lowercase, no full stop.
Git tab, toolbar: what the undo button would take back, shown after "Undo: ". {count} files were taken out of the next commit again. Lowercase, no full stop.
Git tab, toolbar: what the undo button would take back, shown after "Undo: ". All staged changes were taken out of the next commit again. Lowercase, no full stop.
Git tab, toolbar: what the undo button would take back, shown after "Undo: ". The changes of one file were thrown away. Lowercase, no full stop.
Git tab, toolbar: what the undo button would take back, shown after "Undo: ". The changes of {count} files were thrown away. Lowercase, no full stop.
Git tab, toolbar: what the undo button would take back, shown after "Undo: ". A commit was made. {title} is its title. Commit is the Git word and stays.
Git tab, toolbar: what the undo button would take back, shown after "Undo: ". A branch was deleted. {name} is its name. Branch is the Git word and stays.
Git tab: headline of the notice when a branch cannot be deleted because it has commits that are in no other branch.
Git tab: explanation of the notice about a branch that is not merged. {branch} is its name. The question is answered by the buttons.
strings.en: {branch} has commits that are in no other branch. Delete it anyway?
strings.de: {branch} hat Commits, die in keinem anderen Branch sind. Trotzdem löschen?

strings.context: Git tab: button of the notice about a branch that is not merged; deletes it anyway. Short.
Git tab: headline of the notice when a pull needs a decision because the local branch and the remote both have new commits.
Git tab: explanation of the notice about a pull on diverged branches. Merge and rebase are Git words and stay; the buttons answer the question.
strings.en: Your branch and the remote both have new commits. Merge them, or put your commits on top of the remote ones (rebase)?
strings.de: Dein Branch und der Remote haben beide neue Commits. Zusammenführen (Merge) oder deine Commits obendrauf setzen (Rebase)?

strings.context: Git tab: button of the pull decision notice that joins the branches with a merge. Merge is the Git word; the German form is a verb. Short.
Git tab: button of the pull decision notice that puts the own commits on top of the remote ones. Rebase is the Git word; the German form is a verb. Short.
Git tab: headline of the notice when a commit was asked for but nothing is staged.
Git tab: explanation of the notice about a commit with nothing staged. Staging means putting changes into the next commit.
strings.en: Stage some changes first, then commit.
strings.de: Merke zuerst Änderungen vor, dann committe.

strings.context: Git tab: headline of the notice when a commit was asked for but its title is empty.
Git tab: explanation of the notice about a commit without a title.
strings.en: Write a short title for the commit first.
strings.de: Schreibe zuerst einen kurzen Titel für den Commit.

strings.context: Git tab: headline of the notice when a merge was to be finished while places are still in conflict.
Git tab: explanation of the notice about conflicts still open. {count} is the number of conflicts left.
strings.en: {count} conflicts are still open. Resolve them first, then continue.
strings.de: Noch {count} Konflikte sind offen. Löse sie zuerst, dann mach weiter.

strings.context: Git tab: headline of the notice when the undo was refused.
Git tab: explanation of the refused undo.
strings.en: Something has changed since then, and undoing it now would lose newer work.
strings.de: Seitdem hat sich etwas geändert, und Rückgängig würde neuere Arbeit verlieren.

strings.context: Git tab: headline of the notice when git does not take a branch name.
Git tab: explanation of a branch name git does not take, also shown under the name field of the new branch dialog. {name} is what the user typed.
strings.en: “{name}” is not a name git accepts for a branch.
strings.de: „{name}“ ist kein Name, den git für einen Branch annimmt.

strings.context: Git tab: headline of the notice when the remote could not be reached.
Git tab: explanation of a remote that could not be reached.
strings.en: The remote could not be reached. Check your network, then try again.
strings.de: Der Remote war nicht erreichbar. Prüfe dein Netzwerk und versuche es noch einmal.

strings.context: Git tab: headline of the notice for an error git reported that has no notice of its own.
Git tab: explanation of an error git reported; the Details button shows what git printed.
strings.en: Git reported an error. The details show what it said.
strings.de: Git hat einen Fehler gemeldet. Die Details zeigen, was es geschrieben hat.

strings.context: Git tab, question dialog before one file of the local changes is discarded: title.
Git tab, question dialog before one file of the local changes is discarded. {name} is the path of the file. Says what is lost and that Undo brings it back; Undo is the name of the toolbar button.
strings.en: The changes in “{name}” are thrown away. Undo can bring them back.
strings.de: Die Änderungen in „{name}“ werden verworfen. Rückgängig kann sie zurückholen.

strings.context: Git tab, question dialog before all not staged local changes are discarded: title.

Git tab, question dialog before all not staged local changes are discarded. {count} is the number of files; new files that git does not track yet are deleted too. Undo is the name of the toolbar button.
strings.en: The changes in {count} files are thrown away, new files are deleted. Undo can bring them back.
strings.de: Die Änderungen in {count} Dateien werden verworfen, neue Dateien gelöscht. Rückgängig kann sie zurückholen.

strings.context: Git tab, question dialog before a local branch is deleted: title.
Git tab, question dialog before a local branch is deleted. {name} is the branch. Undo is the name of the toolbar button.
strings.en: The branch “{name}” is deleted. Undo can bring it back.
strings.de: Der Branch „{name}“ wird gelöscht. Rückgängig kann ihn zurückholen.

strings.context: Git tab, question dialog before a branch is deleted on the remote server: title.
Git tab, question dialog before a branch is deleted on the remote server. {branch} is the branch, {remote} the remote. Warns that it cannot be undone. Undo is the name of the toolbar button.
strings.en: The branch “{branch}” is deleted on “{remote}” for everyone who uses it. Undo cannot bring it back.
strings.de: Der Branch „{branch}“ wird auf „{remote}“ für alle gelöscht, die ihn nutzen. Rückgängig kann ihn nicht zurückholen.

strings.context: Git tab, question dialog before a stash is deleted: title. A stash is a set of changes put aside.
Git tab, question dialog before a stash is deleted. {name} is the message of the stash. Warns that it cannot be undone. Undo is the name of the toolbar button.
strings.en: The stash “{name}” and the changes in it are lost. Undo cannot bring it back.
strings.de: Der Stash „{name}“ und die Änderungen darin gehen verloren. Rückgängig kann ihn nicht zurückholen.

strings.context: Git tab, confirm button of the discard questions. Short.
Git tab, confirm button of the delete questions (branch, branch on the remote, stash). Short.
Git tab, dialog that renames a local branch: title.
Git tab, rename dialog: label above the field with the new name of the branch.
Git tab, rename dialog: confirm button. Short.
Command list: heading of the Git commands, offered while a Git tab is shown. git is the name of the program.
Command list, Git group: takes back the last local Git action of the tab.
Command list, Git group: commits the staged files with the message typed in the tab.
Command list, Git group: merges the branch chosen in the left list into the current branch.
strings.en: Merge the chosen branch into the current one
strings.de: Gewählten Branch in den aktuellen mergen

strings.context: Command list, Git group: rebases the current branch onto the branch chosen in the left list.
strings.en: Rebase the current branch onto the chosen one
strings.de: Aktuellen Branch auf den gewählten rebasen

strings.context: Command list, Git group: applies the stash chosen in the left list and keeps it. A stash is a set of changes put aside.
Command list, Git group: applies the stash chosen in the left list and deletes it.
strings.en: Apply the chosen stash and delete it

strings.context: Command list, Git group: brings the conflict markers of the chosen file back and throws its resolution away.
strings.en: Reset the resolution of the chosen file

strings.context: Entry of the feature list on the settings tab, only in the App Store build while the free trial or the purchase matters: the page about the 14-day trial and the one-time purchase of the full version.

Line under the heading of the Full version page on the settings tab of the App Store build. The page shows the state of the trial and the buttons to start it, buy the full version and restore an earlier purchase.
strings.en: Your trial and the one-time purchase of ncrs.
strings.de: Dein Testzeitraum und der einmalige Kauf von ncrs.

strings.context: Label of the row on the Full version page that says where the trial or the purchase stands. The value beside it is one of the status sentences.
Label of the row on the Full version page with the button that starts the free 14-day trial of the App Store build.
Label of the row on the Full version page with the button that buys the full version of ncrs once in the App Store.
Label of the row on the Full version page with the button that asks the App Store for earlier purchases of ncrs, for instance after a new computer.
Button on the Full version page that starts the free trial period of 14 days in the App Store build.
Button on the Full version page that starts the one-time purchase of the full version through the App Store.
Button on the Full version page that asks the App Store to give back an earlier purchase of ncrs.
Status on the Full version page while the free trial has not been started yet.
Status on the Full version page during the trial. The placeholder {days} is the number of days left, two or more.
Status on the Full version page during the trial when exactly one day is left (singular form of the trial status).
Status on the Full version page and in the notice of a locked action once the 14-day trial has run out.
Status on the Full version page after the one-time purchase of the full version in the App Store.
Status on the Full version page for people who bought ncrs when it still cost money. Their purchase unlocks everything without a new one.
Sentence on the Full version page about the model: one payment, no subscription, and what stays free after the trial has ended.
strings.en: One-time purchase, no subscription. After the trial you can still view, browse and search your files; changing them needs the full version.
strings.de: Einmaliger Kauf, kein Abo. Nach dem Testzeitraum kannst du Dateien weiter ansehen, durchsuchen und durchblättern; Ändern braucht die Vollversion.

strings.context: Notice when an action that changes files is refused because the free trial of the App Store build was never started.
strings.en: Start the free trial or buy the full version.
strings.de: Starte den kostenlosen Testzeitraum oder kaufe die Vollversion.

strings.context: Notice of a refused action with the pointer that opens the Full version page. The placeholder {reason} is the sentence that says why the action did not run.
Hint in the status bar during the last days of the trial, pressing it opens the Full version page. The placeholder {days} is the number of days left, two or more.
Hint in the status bar when exactly one day of the trial is left (singular form of the status bar hint).
Hint in the status bar after the trial has ended, pressing it opens the Full version page.
Notice after a purchase that the App Store holds back, for instance for an approval by a family organizer. The unlock follows by itself.
strings.en: The purchase is waiting for approval. ncrs unlocks when it goes through.
strings.de: Der Kauf wartet auf eine Freigabe. ncrs schaltet frei, sobald sie da ist.

strings.context: Notice when the App Store could not finish a purchase or the restore. The placeholder {error} is the reason the store gave.
strings.en: The App Store could not finish this: {error}
strings.de: Der App Store konnte das nicht abschließen: {error}

strings.context: Notice after Restore purchase when the App Store knows of no earlier purchase of ncrs for this Apple account.
strings.en: No earlier purchase was found for this Apple account.
strings.de: Für dieses Apple-Konto wurde kein früherer Kauf gefunden.

strings.context: Git tab and repository list: chip that says the branch is behind its upstream. {upstream} is the name of the remote branch, for example origin/main. The number of commits is shown next to it with an arrow, not in this text.
Git tab and repository list: chip that says the branch has commits the upstream does not have yet, so a push is due. Lower case, one word. The number of commits is shown next to it with an arrow.
Git tab and repository list: chip for exactly one file with local, uncommitted changes. {count} is 1.
Git tab and repository list: chip for several files with local, uncommitted changes. {count} is 2 or more.
Git tab and repository list: chip for exactly one file with a merge conflict. {count} is 1.
Git tab and repository list: chip for several files with a merge conflict. {count} is 2 or more.
Git tab and repository list: chip of a branch that has nothing to fetch or push and no local changes. Lower case, short.
Repository list: word next to the spinner of a repository whose fetch or pull is running right now. Lower case, one word.
Repository list: result word for a repository whose fetch or pull brought new commits. Lower case, one word.
Repository list: result word for a repository whose fetch or pull found nothing new. Lower case.
Repository list: result word for a repository that was left out of a run, for example because it has local changes or no upstream. Lower case, one word.
Repository list: result word for a repository whose fetch or pull failed. Lower case, one word.
Tooltip of the thin bar between two panes of a page that can be dragged to change a pane's width.
strings.en: Drag to change the width · double-click resets
strings.de: Ziehen ändert die Breite · Doppelklick setzt zurück

strings.context: Small label that follows the mouse while a pane's width is dragged. {width} is the width in pixels. Keep px.
Repository list: note on a row whose folder is not there any more or cannot be read, shown dimmed. Lower case.
Git tab header: small label above the name of the open repository, which is also the button that opens the list of repositories. Keep the word Repository.
Git tab header: small label above the name of the checked-out branch, which is also the button that opens the list of branches.
Git tab: placeholder of the search field at the top of the branch list.
Git tab: placeholder of the search field at the top of the repository list.
Git tab, commit list: title of the first row, which stands for the changes in the folder that are not committed yet (work in progress). Short.
Git tab, commit list: part of the first row after its title, the number of files with changes. {count} is the number. Lower case, short.
Git tab, commit list: part of the first row after the number of changed files, the number of files already staged for the next commit. {count} is the number. Lower case, short.
Git tab, commit list: in the column of the commit id on the first row, which has no commit yet. Abbreviation of work in progress, upper case, three letters.
Column head of the repository list: the name of the repository folder.
Column head of the repository list: the folder the repository lies in, shown with its start cut off.
Column head of the repository list: the branch that is checked out.
Column head of the repository list: whether the branch is behind or ahead of its upstream.
Column head of the repository list: the files with local changes or conflicts.
Column head of the repository list: when the repository was last fetched from its remote.
Start of the result bar after a fetch or pull over one repository, followed by what happened to it. {count} is 1. Ends with a colon.
Start of the result bar after a fetch or pull over several repositories, followed by what happened to them. {count} is at least 2. Ends with a colon.
Shown in the group column of the Git actions in the keyboard shortcuts dialog. The name of the Git tab; keep Git.
Note under the list of the keyboard shortcuts dialog: the keys of its Git actions cannot be changed here. [keys.git] is the name of a table in the config file; keep it as it is.
strings.en: The Git keys are shown only. Change them in the [keys.git] table of the config file.
strings.de: Die Git-Tasten sind nur zur Ansicht. Man ändert sie in der Tabelle [keys.git] der Konfigurationsdatei.

strings.context: Git tab, toolbar: what the undo button would take back, shown after "Undo: ". A pattern was added to the ignore file. {pattern} is the pattern, e.g. *.log.
Git tab, toolbar: what the undo button would take back, shown after "Undo: ". A tag was created. {name} is its name. Tag is the Git word and stays.
Git tab, toolbar: what the undo button would take back, shown after "Undo: ". A commit was copied onto the branch (cherry-pick). {title} is its title. Cherry-pick is the Git word and stays.

Git tab, toolbar: what the undo button would take back, shown after "Undo: ". A commit was reverted, that is a new commit undoes its changes. {title} is the title of the reverted commit. Revert is the Git word and stays.

Git tab, toolbar: what the undo button would take back, shown after "Undo: ". A branch was moved to another commit (reset). {branch} is the branch, {sha} the short id of the commit it was moved to. Reset is the Git word and stays.
Git tab, toolbar: what the undo button would take back, shown after "Undo: ". Several branches were deleted together by the clean up. {count} is how many, at least 1.
Git tab, branch list: small heading over the branches of this computer. Shown in upper case.
Git tab, branch list: small heading over the branches that live on a server (remote). Shown in upper case.
Git tab, branch list: last row, it starts a new branch at the commit that is checked out instead of switching. The key of the action is shown at its right.
Git tab, open picker list, hint under the rows after the key caps up/down arrow: moves the highlight. One or two words.
Git tab, open repository list, hint after the Enter key cap: opens the highlighted repository.
Git tab, open branch list, hint after the Enter key cap: switches to the highlighted branch (checkout).
Git tab, open branch list, hint after the Cmd+Enter key cap: puts the local changes aside (stash) and then switches to the highlighted branch.
Git tab, open picker list, hint after the Esc key cap: closes the list.

Git tab, header: dim text after the state chips, the folder of the worktree that this tab shows. {path} is the folder, written with ~ for the home folder. Worktree is the Git word for a second working folder of one repository.
Git tab, toolbar button that asks for the name of a new branch. One word.
Git tab, tooltip of the locked Undo button: there is no Git action of this tab to take back.
Git tab, detail pane, label of a fact line: who wrote the commit. The name and the date follow. One word.
Git tab, detail pane, label of a fact line: who committed it, shown only when that differs from the author (after a cherry-pick or rebase).
Git tab, detail pane, label of a fact line: the commit before this one, shown as a link that jumps to it.
Git tab, detail pane, label of a fact line of a merge commit: the commits before it, each a link that jumps to it.
Git tab, detail pane, label of a fact line: the short id of the commit, with the key that copies the full one. SHA is the Git word and stays.
Git tab, detail pane, label of a fact line: the branches that contain this commit, as chips.
Git tab, right end of the status line after the key that copies the id of the commit. {sha} is the short id.
Git tab: status line while a picker list in the header is open. Keep the key names as they are on the keyboard.
strings.en: Type to search · ↑↓ choose · Enter confirms · Esc closes the list
strings.de: Tippen sucht · ↑↓ wählen · Enter bestätigt · Esc schließt die Liste

strings.context: Git tab: status line while a splitter bar between two panes has the keys. Keep the key names as they are on the keyboard.
strings.en: ←→ move the bar by 16 px · ⇧←→ by 64 px · Home standard width · Tab next area · Esc closes
strings.de: ←→ Balken um 16 px · ⇧←→ um 64 px · Pos1 Standardbreite · Tab nächster Bereich · Esc schließt

strings.context: Git tab: status line while the commit list has the keys. {head} jumps to the checked-out commit, {wip} to the local changes, {parent} to the parent commit, {copy} copies the SHA; each is the key as written on the keyboard.
strings.en: ↑↓ choose · Enter to the files · {head} HEAD · {wip} local changes · {parent} parent · {copy} copy SHA · Space mark for compare · Tab next area · / filter · Esc closes
strings.de: ↑↓ wählen · Enter zu den Dateien · {head} HEAD · {wip} lokale Änderungen · {parent} Eltern · {copy} SHA kopieren · Leertaste markiert zum Vergleich · Tab nächster Bereich · / Filter · Esc schließt

strings.context: Command list (F1), Git tab: opens the list of repositories in the header.
Command list (F1), Git tab: opens the list of branches in the header, to switch to one.
Command list (F1), Git tab: puts the cursor of the commit list on the commit that is checked out (HEAD).
Command list (F1), Git tab: goes to the local changes that are not committed yet (WIP).
Command list (F1), Git tab: copies the full id (SHA) of the chosen commit.
Command list (F1), Git tab: jumps to the parent commit of the chosen commit.
Command list (F1), Git tab: switches the file list of the detail pane between a list of paths and a tree of folders.
Heading of the Repos tab and its tab title; the tab lists every Git repository on this computer.
Line next to the heading of the Repos tab: how many repositories there are, how many have local changes and how many are behind their remote.
Button in the Repos tab that searches the project folders for repositories now.
The same button while the search runs; pressing it again stops the search.
Button in the Repos tab that opens a folder dialog to add one repository by hand.
Placeholder of the filter field in the Repos tab; typing narrows the list by name or folder.
Count of the repositories that are ticked in the Repos tab, shown in the bar of the bulk actions.
Tick box in the toolbar of the Repos tab, also the name of the action in the command list: when off, the worktrees of a repository are not listed under it.
Column head in the list of the Repos tab while a bulk action runs or its result is shown: what the action did to the repository. Replaces the head Cleanable. One word.
Tick box in the Repos tab: shows only repositories that are behind, ahead or have local changes.
Button and menu entry in the Repos tab: opens each ticked repository in a Git tab of its own.
Title of the first group of the Repos list: the repositories marked with a star.
Title of the group of the Repos list with the repositories that are shown in a Git tab right now.
Title of the group of the Repos list with repositories whose folder is gone or cannot be read.
Title of a group of the Repos list: the repositories the search found below this project folder.
Title of the group of the Repos list with repositories added by hand or learned from a file panel.
strings.en: Added by hand or from a panel
strings.de: Von Hand oder aus einem Panel hinzugefügt

strings.context: Bulk action button and command in the Repos tab: switches each repository to its default branch.
Bulk action button and command in the Repos tab: pulls each repository, only when no merge is needed (fast-forward).
Bulk action button and command in the Repos tab: switches to the default branch, then pulls it fast-forward.
Button in the result bar of a bulk action in the Repos tab: runs the action again on the repositories that failed.
Button in the result bar of a bulk action: shows only the repositories that were skipped or failed.
The same button after it was pressed: shows the result of every repository again.
Text in the empty Repos list: no repository found yet, with the way to get some.
strings.en: No repositories yet. Add a project folder in Settings → Git or add a repository by hand.
strings.de: Noch keine Repositories. Lege in den Einstellungen unter Git einen Projektordner fest oder füge eins von Hand hinzu.

strings.context: Result of a bulk action for a repository whose folder does not exist any more.
Message in the Repos tab when the list of repositories could not be written to its file; the reason follows.
strings.de: Die Liste konnte nicht gespeichert werden: {reason}

strings.context: Message in the Repos tab when its list file repos.toml is damaged; the file is kept as it is and nothing is saved to it. The reason is what the parser said.
strings.en: repos.toml could not be read and stays unchanged, nothing is saved: {reason}
strings.de: repos.toml ist nicht lesbar und bleibt unverändert, nichts wird gespeichert: {reason}

strings.context: Message in the Repos tab when its list file repos.toml was written by a newer version of ncrs; the file is kept as it is.
strings.en: repos.toml comes from a newer ncrs and stays unchanged, nothing is saved
strings.de: repos.toml stammt von einem neueren ncrs und bleibt unverändert, nichts wird gespeichert

strings.context: Message in the Repos tab when the folder picked to add is not inside a Git repository.
Command in the command list (F1), Repos tab: ticks every repository of the list, or none when all are ticked.
Menu entry and command in the Repos tab: marks the repository as a favourite or takes the star away.
Button, menu entry and command in the Repos tab: takes a repository, whose folder is gone, off the list.
Menu entry in the Repos tab: shows the repository in a Git tab.
Menu entry and command in the Repos tab: shows the folder of the repository in the active file panel (the two-panel file view) and switches to it.
Column of the Repos list that shows when a repository last fetched: the repository never did.
Hint in the status bar of the Repos tab: nothing runs until a button of the bulk actions is pressed.
strings.en: Nothing is changed until you press an action. Space ticks, * marks a favourite.
strings.de: Nichts wird geändert, bis du eine Aktion drückst. Leertaste wählt, * markiert einen Favoriten.

strings.context: Hint in the status bar of the Repos tab after a bulk action ended: Escape closes the result.
Status bar of the Repos tab while a bulk action runs: how many repositories are done and how many run now.
Title of the log line under the list of the Repos tab while or after a bulk action.
Log line of the Repos tab before the first command of a bulk action has ended.
Short name of the Repos tab at the left of its status bar, in capitals.
Result column of a bulk action in the Repos tab: this repository is being worked on.
Result column of a bulk action in the Repos tab: the repository was updated by this many commits.
Result column of the Push bulk action in the Repos tab: the repository's branch was pushed, this many commits went to the remote (0 for a branch that had no remote branch yet).
Result column of a bulk action in the Repos tab: there was nothing to update.
Result column of a bulk action in the Repos tab: the branch was switched, then this many commits taken over.
Result column of a bulk action in the Repos tab: a linked worktree is left alone.
Result column of a bulk action in the Repos tab: skipped because of this many files with local changes.
Result column of a bulk action in the Repos tab: skipped because no branch is checked out (Git: detached HEAD), switching could lose commits.
Result column of a bulk action in the Repos tab: skipped because the repository's own Git config has content filters (git-crypt, Git LFS), which bulk actions do not run.
Result column of a bulk push in the Repos tab: skipped because the branch exists only locally; the bulk push does not publish new branches.
Result column of a bulk action in the Repos tab: skipped because the branch has own commits and would need a merge.
strings.en: {n} own commits, needs a merge, skipped

strings.context: Result column of a bulk action in the Repos tab: the remote asked for a login, which background runs never give.
Result column of a bulk action in the Repos tab: the command failed; the log line shows what git said.
Name of the Git page in the list of settings pages: where the Repos tab searches and how bulk actions behave.
Intro text at the top of the Git settings page, above the groups of settings.
strings.en: Where ncrs looks for Git repositories, what it leaves out, and how the actions on many repositories behave.
strings.de: Wo ncrs nach Git-Repositories sucht, was es auslässt und wie sich die Aktionen auf mehrere Repositories verhalten.

strings.context: Title of the group on the Git settings page that lists the project folders searched for repositories.
Title of the group on the Git settings page with how deep and where the search looks.
Title of the group on the Git settings page with the places and folder names the search does not enter.
Title of the group on the Git settings page with how the actions on many repositories behave.
Text under the empty list of project folders on the Git settings page.
strings.en: No project folder yet. Add the folder that holds your repositories.
strings.de: Noch kein Projektordner. Füge den Ordner hinzu, in dem deine Repositories liegen.

strings.context: Button on the Git settings page that starts the search for repositories right away.
Label of the switch on the Git settings page that adds the home folder to the places searched.
Note under the switch to search the home folder: it happens once at the first start of the Repos tab.
strings.en: Once when the Repos tab opens for the first time, then only when you ask.
strings.de: Einmal beim ersten Öffnen des Repos-Tabs, danach nur auf Wunsch.

strings.context: Label of the choice on the Git settings page: how many folder levels below a project folder the search goes.
Note under the search depth choice: what a level is.
strings.en: Folder levels below a project folder. Deeper takes longer.
strings.de: Ordnerebenen unter einem Projektordner. Tiefer dauert länger.

strings.context: Label of the switch on the Git settings page: repositories opened in a file panel join the Repos list.
Note under the switch to learn repositories from the panels: what happens to a repository that is entered.
strings.en: A repository you enter in a panel is added to the list.
strings.de: Ein Repository, in das du in einem Panel gehst, kommt in die Liste.

strings.context: Label of the switch on the Git settings page: the search does not enter folders of cloud storage.
Note under the switch to skip cloud folders: why, since entering them can download files.
strings.en: iCloud, OneDrive, Dropbox and the like: entering them can start downloads.
strings.de: iCloud, OneDrive, Dropbox und ähnliche: Hineingehen kann Downloads auslösen.

strings.context: Label of the switch on the Git settings page: the search does not enter network drives.
Note under the switch to skip network drives: why, since they can be slow or asleep.
strings.en: Network drives can be slow or not there at all.
strings.de: Netzlaufwerke können langsam sein oder gar nicht da.

strings.context: Label of an info row on the Git settings page: which branch the action to the default branch switches to.
Value of the default branch info row: it is read from each repository, not set here.
Label of the choice on the Git settings page: how many repositories an action works on at the same time.
Note under the concurrency choice: more is faster but loads the network and the disk.
strings.en: Repositories handled in parallel by one action.
strings.de: Repositories, die eine Aktion gleichzeitig bearbeitet.

strings.context: Title of the group on the Git settings page with what a pull does when the branches have diverged.
Title of the group on the Git settings page with the fetch the Git tab does in the background.
Label of the choice on the Git settings page: how a pull joins the fetched commits when the branches have diverged.
Note under the pull choice on the Git settings page: the Pull menu of the Git tab can pick another way for a single pull.
strings.en: The Pull menu picks another way for a single pull.
strings.de: Das Pull-Menü wählt für einen einzelnen Pull einen anderen Weg.

strings.context: Option of the pull choice on the Git settings page: join with a merge commit. Keep it short, it is a button.
Option of the pull choice on the Git settings page: put the own commits on top of the fetched ones. Keep it short, it is a button.
Option of the pull choice on the Git settings page: only move the branch forward, ask when that is not possible. Keep it short, it is a button.
Label of the choice on the Git settings page: how often the Git tab fetches the repositories you opened.
Note under the fetch choice on the Git settings page: a fetch only downloads, it changes no branch and no file.
strings.en: Only fetches; it changes no branch and no file.
strings.de: Holt nur, ändert nichts an Branches oder Dateien.

strings.context: Option of the fetch choice on the Git settings page: never fetch in the background. Keep it short, it is a button.
Option of the fetch choice on the Git settings page: fetch every 15 minutes. Keep it short, it is a button.
Option of the fetch choice on the Git settings page: fetch every hour. Keep it short, it is a button.
Label of an info row on the Git settings page: what an action does with repositories that have local changes.
Value of the local changes info row: such repositories are skipped, never touched.
Button in the Repos tab that opens the dialog to clone a repository from an address into a folder.
Title of the dialog in the Repos tab that clones a repository from an address.
Label above the address field of the clone dialog in the Repos tab: where the repository comes from.
Placeholder of the address field of the clone dialog in the Repos tab; the address may be https or ssh.
Label of the folder in the clone dialog of the Repos tab: the folder that gets a new folder for the clone, followed by the button to choose another one.
