Button in the clone dialog of the Repos tab that opens a folder dialog to choose the folder the clone goes into.
Confirm button of the clone dialog in the Repos tab; Enter presses it. Verb, imperative.
Line in the clone dialog of the Repos tab while git copies the repository; the dialog cannot be closed until it ends. Placeholder is the address.
Problem line in the clone dialog of the Repos tab when the chosen folder does not exist. Placeholder is the folder.
Column head in the list of the Repos tab: how many merged branches and worktrees a repository has that can be deleted. Short, one word.
Title of the shut Keep section of the clean-up pane of the Repos tab: what is never offered. The number of entries stands beside it.
Quiet line under the list of the Repos tab that explains the Cleanable column.
strings.en: Cleanable counts branches and worktrees already merged into the default branch. Branches merged on the server show up once Clean up has fetched.
strings.de: Aufräumbar zählt Branches und Worktrees, die schon im Standard-Branch sind. Auf dem Server gemergte Branches kommen dazu, sobald Aufräumen geholt hat.

strings.context: Button in the bar of the bulk actions of the Repos tab: opens the pane that deletes merged branches and worktrees. The dots say that a pane asks first.
Entry of the command list while the Repos tab is shown: takes the last clean-up back, brings the deleted branches back. Only works while the clean-up pane is open.
Entry of the command list while the Repos tab is shown: opens the clean-up of merged branches and worktrees over the chosen repositories.
strings.en: Clean up merged branches and worktrees…

strings.context: In front of the bulk action buttons of the Repos tab: what they run on. {what} is the name of the repository under the cursor, or a count such as "6 selected" or "5 favourites".

Added to the label of a bulk action button of the Repos tab when nothing is ticked and there are no favourites: the action runs on the repository of the row under the cursor. Also under the title of the clean-up pane.
Added to the label of a bulk action button of the Repos tab when nothing is ticked and the action runs on the favourites. {n} is how many.
Heading of the clean-up pane of the Repos tab. {count} is the number of repositories it covers.
First paragraph of the clean-up pane of the Repos tab: what happens when it opens. fetch --prune is a git command and stays.
strings.en: Fetches every chosen repo (fetch --prune), then lists merged branches and worktrees. Nothing is deleted without a tick.
strings.de: Holt alle gewählten Repos (fetch --prune), dann listet es gemergte Branches und Worktrees. Ohne Haken wird nichts gelöscht.

strings.context: Line in the clean-up pane of the Repos tab while the repositories are fetched and read. {done} of {total} repositories are finished.
Summary line of the clean-up pane of the Repos tab: what can be deleted. Placeholders are counts.
Right of the summary line of the clean-up pane of the Repos tab: the time of day the fetch ended. {time} is hours and minutes.
Warning in the clean-up pane of the Repos tab: fetching one repository failed, so its list is the state of the last fetch. {repo} is the name, {reason} the last line git said.
strings.en: {repo}: fetch failed, showing the state of the last fetch ({reason})
strings.de: {repo}: Holen fehlgeschlagen, Stand des letzten Holens ({reason})

strings.context: Warning in the clean-up pane of the Repos tab: a repository could not be read at all. {repo} is the name, {reason} what went wrong.
Under the name of a shut repository group in the clean-up pane of the Repos tab: what is inside. Placeholders are counts.
Line in the clean-up pane of the Repos tab: the repositories that have nothing to delete. {repos} is a comma separated list of names.
Text under the shut Keep section of the clean-up pane of the Repos tab: what is never offered. {example} is empty or the text of repos.cleanup_keep_example.
strings.en: Current branch, the default branch, new branches without commits, branches with commits that are neither pushed nor merged{example}, worktrees with local changes.
strings.de: Aktueller Branch, Standard-Branch, neue Branches ohne Commits, Branches mit Commits, die weder gepusht noch gemergt sind{example}, Worktrees mit lokalen Änderungen.

strings.context: Example inside the Keep text of the clean-up pane of the Repos tab, with a leading space and in brackets. {example} is repository, branch and reason.
Checkbox in the clean-up pane of the Repos tab: also delete the branch on the server, not only the local one.
Under the remote checkbox of the clean-up pane of the Repos tab: only branches that are in the default branch are deleted there. {count} branches on {remote}.
strings.en: only those in the default branch, {count} on {remote}
strings.de: nur die im Standard-Branch enthaltenen, {count} auf {remote}

strings.context: Quiet line in the clean-up pane of the Repos tab: what Undo does after deleting, and until when. Deleted remote branches and worktree folders are not brought back.
strings.en: Undo brings deleted branches back as long as the tab is open.
strings.de: Rückgängig holt gelöschte Branches zurück, solange der Tab offen ist.

strings.context: Button in the clean-up pane of the Repos tab that leaves without deleting anything; the key name Esc follows it, so it stays short.
Quiet line under the buttons of the clean-up pane in the Repos tab: the deletes report like the bulk actions do, one result per repository.
strings.en: Runs like the bulk actions: a result per repo.
strings.de: Läuft wie die Sammelaktion: Ergebnis je Repo.

strings.context: Red button of the clean-up pane of the Repos tab: deletes what is ticked. {count} branches and worktrees in {repos} repositories.
Right side of the status bar while the clean-up pane of the Repos tab is open: how many of the offered entries are ticked.
Status bar hint while the clean-up pane of the Repos tab is open: the keys that work in it.
strings.en: Up/Down choose · Space tick · Left/Right shut/open repo · Tab list/clean-up · Enter deletes · Esc closes
strings.de: Hoch/Runter wählen · Leertaste Haken · Links/Rechts Repo zu/auf · Tab Liste/Aufräumen · Enter löscht · Esc schließt

strings.context: Result next to an entry of the clean-up pane of the Repos tab after it was deleted. Lowercase, one word.
Summary line of the clean-up pane of the Repos tab after the deleting ended. {count} entries were deleted.
Button in the clean-up pane of the Repos tab after deleting: brings the deleted branches back.
Summary line of the clean-up pane of the Repos tab after Undo. {count} branches are back.
Warning in the clean-up pane of the Repos tab: Undo failed in one repository. {repo} is the name, {reason} what git said.
Reason in the clean-up lists (Git tab and Repos tab) why a branch can be deleted: everything on it is in the default branch. {main} is its name, usually main.
Reason in the clean-up lists why a branch can be deleted: its pull request was merged and the branch on the server is gone. Short, fits a narrow column.
Reason in the clean-up lists why a worktree can be deleted: nothing but the worktree goes, its branch is merged. Short, fits a narrow column.
Reason in the clean-up lists why a branch is never offered: it is the default branch of the repository.
Reason in the clean-up lists why a branch is never offered: it is checked out in the repository.
Reason in the clean-up lists why a branch is never offered: it was just made and holds no commit of its own yet.
Reason in the clean-up lists why a branch is never offered: it holds one commit that is neither merged nor pushed.
Reason in the clean-up lists why a branch is never offered: it holds {count} commits that are neither merged nor pushed.
Reason in the clean-up lists why a branch is never offered: it is pushed but not merged into the default branch.
Reason in the clean-up lists why a branch is never offered: its remote branch is gone but it got commits after the last push, or the state before is unknown.
Reason in the clean-up lists why a worktree is never offered: it has {count} local changes (edited or new files).
Reason in the clean-up lists why a folder is never offered: it is the main worktree, the repository itself.
Reason in the clean-up lists why a folder is never offered: it is the worktree that is open.
Reason in the clean-up lists why a worktree is never offered: it has no branch checked out (detached head).
Reason in the clean-up lists why a worktree is never offered: it is locked with git worktree lock.
Reason in the clean-up lists why a branch is never offered: it is checked out in a worktree that stays.
Result next to an entry of the clean-up lists that could not be deleted. {reason} is the last line git said.

Second line of a worktree in the clean-up lists when its folder holds files git ignores: they are deleted with it. {folder} is the folder name, {files} up to two file names and how many more. Short, fits a narrow column.
The first two ignored files of a worktree, then how many more there are. {names} is a comma separated list of file names, {count} the number left out.
Label of an info row on the Git settings page: when the last search for repositories ran and what it found.
Value of the info row of the last search on the Git settings page. Placeholders are the time (relative, like 'yesterday'), the number of repositories found and the duration in milliseconds.
Value of the info row of the last search on the Git settings page while no search has run yet.
Entry of the command list that runs the key action repos: it opens the Repos tab with the list of all repositories. Also the label of the tab in the tab strip. Noun, plural.
Git tab, commit list: the date column of the first row, which stands for the changes not committed yet. Short, lower case.
Git tab, right pane of the local changes: headline before the branch name, which is shown as a chip after it.
Git tab, right pane of the local changes: how many files are changed and how many of them are staged (put into the next commit). {changed} and {staged} are numbers.
Git tab, right pane of the local changes: the folder of the worktree the changes are in. Worktree is the Git word. {path} is a folder path.
Git tab, local changes: text in the empty list of staged files. Staging means putting a change into the next commit. The key is the space bar.
strings.en: Nothing staged yet. Space stages the chosen file.
strings.de: Noch nichts vorgemerkt. Leertaste merkt die gewählte Datei vor.

strings.context: Git tab, commit box: the length of the commit title at the right end of its field, like 12/72. {count} is the number of characters typed, {limit} the length after which it turns red.
Git tab, commit box: a checkbox. When on, the commit is sent to the remote repository right after it is made.
Git tab, command list (F1): commits the staged files and pushes the branch afterwards. Push is the Git word.
Git tab, entry of the menu behind the Pull button: pull and join with a merge commit. Merge is the Git word.
Git tab, entry of the menu behind the Pull button: pull and put the own commits on top. Rebase is the Git word.
Git tab, entry of the menu behind the Pull button: pull only when the branch can just move forward, otherwise stop.
Git tab, note at the right of the entry of the Pull menu that the Pull button itself does (the default from the settings).
Git tab, entry of the menu behind the Push button: the normal push. Push is the Git word.
Git tab, entry of the menu behind the Push button: replaces the branch on the remote, but only while nobody pushed there since the last look. It asks first.
Git tab, command list (F1): opens the menu with the ways to pull (merge, rebase, fast-forward only).
Git tab, command list (F1): opens the menu with the ways to push.
Git tab, command list (F1): pull and join the fetched commits with a merge.
Git tab, command list (F1): pull and put the local commits on top of the fetched ones (rebase).
Git tab, command list (F1): pull only when the branch can simply move forward, no merge commit.
Git tab, Push menu: why Force push with lease is greyed out. HEAD is not on a branch. Short, shown at the right of the entry.
Git tab, Push menu: why Force push with lease is greyed out. The branch has no upstream yet. Short, shown at the right of the entry.
Git tab, command list (F1): force push with lease; it asks before anything is sent.
Git tab, title of the question before a force push. {remote} and {branch} are the names of the remote and the branch, kept as they are.
Git tab, text of the question before a force push that loses commits. {count} is the number of commits on the remote that the local branch does not have.
strings.en: Your {branch} replaces {remote}/{branch}. {count} commits on the remote that you do not have are lost there. If someone pushes before you confirm, nothing is overwritten.
strings.de: Dein {branch} ersetzt {remote}/{branch}. {count} Commits auf dem Remote, die du nicht hast, gehen dort verloren. Pusht vorher jemand, wird nichts überschrieben.

strings.context: Git tab, text of the question before a force push that loses no commit.
strings.en: Your {branch} replaces {remote}/{branch}. No commits are lost.
strings.de: Dein {branch} ersetzt {remote}/{branch}. Es gehen keine Commits verloren.

strings.context: Git tab, the button that does the force push. Keep it short.
Git tab, title of the notice when a force push with lease stopped because the remote branch moved.
Git tab, text of the notice when a force push with lease stopped because someone pushed to the remote after the last look. Nothing was overwritten.
strings.en: Someone pushed to the remote branch after you looked. Nothing was overwritten. Fetch, look at the new commits, then try again.
strings.de: Nach deinem letzten Blick hat jemand auf den Remote-Branch gepusht. Nichts wurde überschrieben. Hol den Stand, sieh dir die neuen Commits an und versuch es noch einmal.

strings.context: Git tab, the button of the notice that the remote changed: fetches the new commits. Keep it short.
Git tab, title of the dialog in which Git asks for a user name during a pull, push or fetch.
strings.en: Git asks for a user name

strings.context: Git tab, title of the dialog in which Git asks for a password or the passphrase of a key during a pull, push or fetch.
Git tab, title of the dialog in which Git or ssh asks a yes or no question, for example whether to trust an unknown server.
Git tab, label above the field of the login dialog where the user name is typed.
Git tab, label above the masked field of the login dialog where the password or passphrase is typed.
Git tab, the question of the login dialog. {prompt} is the text Git printed, for example the user name it wants for a server; keep it as it is.
Git tab, note in the login dialog: the app only passes the answer on.
strings.en: ncrs hands the answer to git and keeps nothing. Your git credential helper may save it.
strings.de: ncrs gibt die Antwort an git weiter und speichert nichts. Dein Git-Credential-Helper merkt sie sich vielleicht.

strings.context: Git tab, the button of the login dialog that hands the typed answer to Git. Keep it short.
Git tab, the button of the login dialog that answers Git's yes/no question about an unknown server with yes. Keep it short.
Git tab, hint line while the menu behind Pull or Push is open.
Git tab, hint line while the login dialog is open.
Git tab, command list (F1): moves the keyboard to the title field of the commit box.
Git tab, command list (F1): adds the chosen file that Git does not know yet to the ignore file (.gitignore).
Git tab, button on a file Git does not know yet: opens a question where the user picks what goes into the ignore file. The three dots mean a question follows.
Git tab, title of the question about ignoring a file. .gitignore is the name of a file; keep it.
Git tab, ignore question: the choice to ignore only this file. {path} is the path of the file.
Git tab, ignore question: the choice to ignore the whole folder the file is in. {folder} is the folder path.
Git tab, ignore question: the choice to ignore all files with the same ending. {ext} is the ending without the dot, like log.
Git tab, button that confirms the ignore question.
Git tab, diff of a change not staged: what is compared. Index is the Git word for the staging area. {path} is the file path; keep a/ and b/ as they are in a Git diff.
Git tab, diff of a staged change: what is compared. HEAD is the Git word for the last commit, Index for the staging area. {path} is the file path; keep a/ and b/.
Git tab, last line under a diff of a change. {count} is the number of lines shown.
Git tab, button in the diff of a change: opens the file in the editor the user has set.
Git tab: status line while the file lists of the local changes have the keyboard. The placeholders are keys as the platform spells them; keep the other key names as they are on the keyboard.
strings.en: ↑↓ choose · Space stage or unstage · Enter diff · {stage_all} stage all · {unstage_all} unstage all · {commit} commit · Tab next area
strings.de: ↑↓ wählen · Leertaste vormerken/zurücknehmen · Enter Diff · {stage_all} alle vormerken · {unstage_all} alle zurücknehmen · {commit} Commit · Tab nächster Bereich

strings.context: Git tab: status line while the commit box has the keyboard. {commit} and {commit_push} are keys as the platform spells them. Keep the key name Esc.
strings.en: {commit} commit · {commit_push} commit and push · Tab next field · Esc leave the field
strings.de: {commit} Commit · {commit_push} Commit und Push · Tab nächstes Feld · Esc Feld verlassen

strings.context: Git tab: status line while the diff of a local change is open. {other_file} is a key as the platform spells it. Keep the other key names.
strings.en: {other_file} other file · Space stage or unstage · F4 editor · Esc back
strings.de: {other_file} andere Datei · Leertaste vormerken/zurücknehmen · F4 Editor · Esc zurück

strings.context: Git tab, sandbox: headline of the one list of changed files, where no staging is possible. Short.
Git tab, toolbar of the diff of a local change: which change (block of changed lines) of the file has the keys. {current} and {total} are numbers.
Git tab, tooltip of the up arrow in the diff toolbar that jumps to the previous change in the file.
Git tab, tooltip of the down arrow in the diff toolbar that jumps to the next change in the file.

Git tab, diff of a local change: tooltip of the grey buttons that stage, unstage or discard one section while 'Ignore white space' is on. They are off because the lines shown are not the ones git would apply.
strings.en: Not possible while white space is ignored: the lines shown are not the ones git would change.
strings.de: Nicht möglich, solange Leerzeichen ignoriert werden: die gezeigten Zeilen sind nicht die, die Git ändern würde.

strings.context: Git tab: status bar, right end, before the number of commits read. Exactly one file has local changes.
Git tab: status bar, right end, before the number of commits read. {count} files have local changes, 2 or more.
Git tab: header of the column with the commit graph (the lines and dots that join the commits). Upper case, short.
Git tab: stands for the branch name in the commit menu and its questions while no branch is checked out (HEAD points at a commit). Short, lower case.
Git tab, context menu of a commit: copies the full commit id to the clipboard.
Git tab, context menu of a commit: checks the commit out without a branch (detached HEAD).
Git tab, context menu of a commit: asks for the name of a new branch that starts at this commit. Keep the ellipsis.
Git tab, context menu of a commit: asks for the name of a tag on this commit. Keep the ellipsis.
Git tab, context menu of a commit: copies the commit onto the checked-out branch. {branch} is that branch's name, or the word for a detached HEAD.
Git tab, context menu of a commit: makes a new commit that takes this commit's changes back.
Git tab, context menu of a commit: opens the submenu that moves the checked-out branch to this commit. {branch} is that branch's name, or the word for a detached HEAD.
Git tab, reset submenu: moves the branch, the changes of the commits stay staged.
Git tab, reset submenu: moves the branch, the changes of the commits stay in the files but are not staged.
Git tab, reset submenu: moves the branch and throws the changes away; asks first. Shown in red. Keep the ellipsis.
Git tab, context menu of a commit: shows what differs between this commit and the files in the folder.
Git tab, context menu of a commit: shows what differs between the commit marked with Space and this one. Off until a commit is marked.
Git tab, question before a hard reset. {branch} is the branch's name, or the word for a detached HEAD.

Git tab, question before a hard reset: what is lost. {branch} the branch, {sha} the short commit id it moves to, {commits} number of commits that are no longer on the branch, {files} number of files with local changes. Undo is the Undo button of the tab.
strings.en: {branch} jumps to {sha}. {commits} commit(s) and {files} local change(s) are lost. Undo can bring them back.
strings.de: {branch} springt auf {sha}. {commits} Commits und {files} lokale Änderung(en) gehen verloren. Rückgängig kann sie zurückholen.

strings.context: Git tab, confirm button of the hard reset question. Shown in red.
Git tab, title of the dialog that asks for a tag name.
Git tab, tag dialog: label of the name field.
Git tab, tag dialog: example in the empty name field.
Git tab, tag dialog: names the commit that gets the tag. {sha} is the short commit id.
Git tab, tag dialog: confirm button.
Git tab, status bar while the commit menu is open. Keep the arrows and the key names.
strings.en: ↑↓ choose · Enter run · → submenu · ← back · Esc closes
strings.de: ↑↓ wählen · Enter ausführen · → Untermenü · ← zurück · Esc schließt

strings.context: Git tab, commit list: small tag on the commit that was marked with Space to compare with. Short, lower case.
Git tab, diff: stands for the files in the folder, as the right side of the arrow in the header of a comparison and in brackets after a path. Lower case.
Git tab, banner while a cherry-pick stopped on conflicts. {sha} is the short id of the commit being copied.
Git tab, banner while a revert stopped on conflicts. {sha} is the short id of the commit being taken back.
Git tab, button and menu entry: shows the commits that changed the file. Short, noun.
Git tab, button and menu entry: shows for every line of the file which commit it comes from. Blame is the Git word for it; keep it where the language has no own word.
Git tab, headline over the list of commits that changed one file. {path} is the path of the file in the repository.
Git tab, in place of the list of commits that changed one file when there is none.
Git tab, history of a file: small note in front of the message of a commit that renamed the file. {old} is the path it had before. Lower case.
Git tab, headline over the lines of a file with the commit each line comes from. {path} is the path of the file, {sha} the short id of the commit the file is taken from, or HEAD.
Git tab, note beside the headline of a blame: the lines shown are those of the last commit.
strings.en: Shows the last commit; local changes are not included
strings.de: Zeigt den Stand des letzten Commits, lokale Änderungen fehlen

strings.context: Git tab, in place of a blame: the file is not text.
Git tab, in place of a blame: the file has more lines or bytes than the app reads.
Git tab, in place of a blame: the path is a symbolic link or a submodule, so it has no lines.
strings.en: A link or submodule has no lines to blame
strings.de: Ein Link oder Submodul hat keine Zeilen für Blame

strings.context: Git tab, in place of a blame: the file is not in the commit the blame would start from.
strings.en: This file is not in the commit yet
strings.de: Diese Datei ist noch nicht im Commit

strings.context: Git tab, second line of the diff toolbar: what is compared with what. {old} and {new} are paths, {old_side} and {new_side} say which state of the file: a short commit id, HEAD or the words for the working copy. Keep a/ and b/ as they are in a Git diff.
Git tab: status line while the history of a file is shown. Keep the arrows and the key names.
strings.en: ↑↓ choose · Enter show diff · Esc back
strings.de: ↑↓ wählen · Enter Diff zeigen · Esc zurück

strings.context: Git tab: status line while the blame of a file is shown. {history} is a key as the platform spells it. Keep the arrows and the other key names.
strings.en: ↑↓ line · Enter commit of the line · {history} history · Esc back
strings.de: ↑↓ Zeile · Enter Commit der Zeile · {history} Historie · Esc zurück

strings.context: Git tab: right end of the status line while a diff is shown. {file} is the name of the file, {added} and {removed} count its changed lines.
Entry of the context menu of a file in a panel: opens the Git tab with the commits that changed the file. Only offered for a file inside a Git repository.
Entry of the context menu of a file in a panel: opens the Git tab with the commit each line of the file comes from. Only offered for a file inside a Git repository.
Entry of the command list and of the shortcut table: the commits that changed the file under the cursor.
Entry of the command list and of the shortcut table: the commit each line of the file under the cursor comes from.
Git tab, tooltip of the clean-up button and entry of the command list: deletes merged branches and worktrees of this repository after a tick each.
strings.en: Clean up merged branches and worktrees…

strings.context: Git tab, title of the clean-up dialog; {name} is the repository.
Git tab, clean-up dialog while it fetches from the remote before it lists anything.
Git tab, clean-up dialog: the fetch did not work, the list shows the state of the last fetch; {reason} is git's message.
strings.en: Fetch failed, showing the state of the last fetch ({reason})
strings.de: Holen fehlgeschlagen, Stand des letzten Holens ({reason})

strings.context: Git tab, clean-up dialog when no branch or worktree can go.
Git tab, clean-up dialog, line over the list: what is offered.
strings.en: Can go: branches {branches}, worktrees {worktrees}. Nothing is deleted without a tick.
strings.de: Kann weg: Branches {branches}, Worktrees {worktrees}. Ohne Haken wird nichts gelöscht.

strings.context: Git tab, clean-up dialog, button that deletes what is ticked; {count} is how many.
Git tab, clean-up dialog while the deletion runs.
Git tab, clean-up dialog, button that closes it after the deletion.
Git tab, hint line while the clean-up dialog is open.
strings.en: ↑↓ choose · Space tick · ←→ shut/open what stays · Tab remote branches · Enter delete · Esc close
strings.de: ↑↓ wählen · Leertaste Haken · ←→ Bleibt zu/auf · Tab Remote-Branches · Enter löscht · Esc schließt

strings.context: Git tab, mark at the right of a local branch whose commits are all in the default branch.
Git tab, line under the branch list that explains the merged mark.
strings.en: ✓ merged: everything is in the default branch; Clean up can delete it.
strings.de: ✓ gemergt: alles ist im Standard-Branch; Aufräumen kann es löschen.

strings.context: Git tab, context menu of a worktree in the left list: deletes its folder after a question.
Git tab, title of the question before a worktree folder is deleted.
Git tab, sentence added to the question before a worktree folder is deleted when it holds files git ignores: they are lost. {files} is up to two file names and how many more.
strings.en: Ignored files in it are lost: {files}.

strings.context: Git tab, question before a worktree folder is deleted; {name} is the folder. Git refuses a folder with local changes; the branch stays.
strings.en: The folder {name} is deleted. The branch stays. Git refuses if the folder has local changes.
strings.de: Der Ordner {name} wird gelöscht. Der Branch bleibt. Git lehnt ab, wenn der Ordner lokale Änderungen hat.

strings.context: Entry of the command list that runs the key action space: it opens the Platz tab, where the user measures the drive and frees space. Ends with an ellipsis because it opens a view that measures first. Verb phrase.
Title of the Platz tab in the tab strip and heading of the tab. Noun, one word. The tab shows what fills the drive and lets the user delete what a tool makes again.
Title of the Platz tab with the drive it measured. {drive} is the name of the drive, e.g. Macintosh HD.
Heading of the Platz tab and of the Hermes card about the drive. Imperative: free up disk space.
Small label in front of the drive name in the header of the Platz tab. Noun: the disk or volume.
Line under the drive name in the Platz tab. {used}, {total} and {free} are sizes such as 814 GB.
Chip in the header of the Platz tab: how much of the drive is free now. {size} is a size such as 78 GB.
Chip in the header of the Platz tab: how much would be free if everything safe were deleted. {size} is a size such as 213 GB.
Status bar line of the Platz tab. {ago} is a short time span such as 2 min, {took} how long the measuring took such as 1 min 12 s.
Status bar line of the Platz tab while it measures the big folders. {size} is what has been found so far.
Status bar line of the Platz tab when some folders could not be read, so the figures may be too low.
strings.en: Measured in part: some folders could not be read
strings.de: Nur zum Teil gemessen: einige Ordner waren nicht lesbar

strings.context: Button in the Platz tab that measures the drive again. Verb phrase.
Button in the Platz tab that opens Hermes to ask about the drive. Ends with an ellipsis because it opens the chat.
Primary button of the Platz tab. Deletes every safe folder for good, after a question. {size} is the total size such as 134 GB.
Same button as space.delete_all_safe without the size, for the command list and a chat card.
Button of the Platz tab and of a Hermes card: removes the merged Git worktrees. {size} is their total size.
Button on the result of the Platz tab: removes the merged worktrees as well, after the safe folders were deleted. {size} is their size.
Button on a Hermes card that opens the Platz tab. Verb phrase.
Button and command in the Platz tab: shows the folder in a file panel. Verb phrase.
Button and command in the Platz tab: deletes only the selected folder for good, not all safe ones. Verb phrase.
Placeholder of the filter field of the Platz tab. The user types part of a name or a path.
Button on a skipped row of the result in the Platz tab: tries that folder again.
Command and button in the Platz tab: tries every skipped folder of the last run again.
Button on the result of the Platz tab that closes the result and shows the list again.
Button on a row of the group "You decide" in the Platz tab; opens the list of what is inside the folder.
Column header over the size bar in the lists of the Platz tab. Noun.
Column header over the folder name in the lists of the Platz tab. Noun.
Column header over what a folder is, for example "Compiler cache", in the Platz tab.
Column header over the check made before deleting, for example "no build is running".
Column header over the share of the drive a folder takes in the Platz tab. Noun.
Column header over the name in the result list of the Platz tab. Noun, one word.
Column header over the place of a folder in the result list of the Platz tab. Noun.
Column header over what became of a folder in the result list of the Platz tab. Noun.
Column header over the reason a file was suggested in the Downloads list of the Platz tab. Noun.
Heading of the group of folders that tools make again, in the Platz tab. Deleting them is safe. Shown in capitals.
Heading of the group of merged Git worktrees in the Platz tab. Shown in capitals.
Heading of the group of the user's own files in the Platz tab. The user decides; Hermes only explains. Shown in capitals.
Heading of the group of folders a running program holds open, in the Platz tab. They are skipped. Shown in capitals.
Heading of the safe group on the result of the Platz tab. Shown in capitals.
Dimmed text after the heading of the safe group on the result: what happened to it.
strings.en: can be rebuilt, deleted for good

strings.context: Dimmed text after the heading "You decide" in the Platz tab. Hermes explains but never deletes by itself.
strings.en: Hermes explains, never deletes here by itself
strings.de: Hermes erklärt, löscht hier nie von selbst

strings.context: Dimmed text after the heading "You decide" on the result of the Platz tab.
Dimmed text after the heading "In use" on the result of the Platz tab: those folders were skipped.
Dimmed text after the heading of the merged worktrees. {folder} is the folder of the worktrees, {total} how many worktrees there are, {size} their size, {kept} how many stay.
Folded row below the list of merged worktrees. {count} is the number not shown, {size} their size.
Word after a folded row in the Platz tab: pressing the arrow key opens it.
Check column of a merged worktree row in the Platz tab: it has no changes and its branch is merged.
Reason column of a merged worktree row in the Platz tab: what removing does.
Legend word under the bar of the drive: the part that is safe to delete. Lower case, short.

strings.context: Heading of a block of the Platz page: how deep the measuring goes. Shown in capitals.
Label of a setting on the Platz page: how many folder levels below home are searched. Noun.
Choice of the depth setting: the app decides.
Note under the depth setting.
strings.en: Auto goes deeper where a lot lies
strings.de: Auto geht tiefer, wo viel liegt

strings.context: Switch on the Platz page: whether other drives are measured too.
Note on the Platz page of the App Store version: access must be granted to folders.
strings.en: App Store version: measures and deletes only in folders you have granted access to. One click on "Grant home folder" covers everything under ~.
strings.de: App-Store-Version: misst und löscht nur in Ordnern, die du freigegeben hast. Ein Klick auf „Benutzerordner freigeben“ reicht für alles unter ~.

strings.context: Button on the Platz page of the App Store version. Ends with an ellipsis because it opens a dialog.
The sentence the Monitor sends to Hermes when the user clicks "Free up space…". It is shown as the user's message.
strings.en: Why is my drive so full?
strings.de: Warum ist meine Platte so voll?

strings.context: Title of a chat that was started from the Platz tab.
strings.en: Why is the drive so full?
strings.de: Warum ist die Platte so voll?

strings.context: Hermes bubble while the Platz measuring runs.
strings.en: I am measuring the big folders…

strings.context: Hermes bubble with the result of the measuring. {used} and {total} and {free} are sizes, {percent} the used share, {took} how long measuring took.
strings.en: {used} of {total} are used, {free} free ({percent} %). I measured the big folders ({took}).
strings.de: Belegt sind {used} von {total}, frei {free} ({percent} %). Ich habe die großen Ordner gemessen ({took}).

strings.context: Heading of the card in the chat: where the space went.
Subheading of the card in the chat. {drive} is the drive name, {total} its size.
Line on the card in the chat. {free} is the free space and {percent} the used share after deleting all safe folders.
Column header on the card in the chat. Noun.
Column header on the card in the chat. Noun.
Column header on the card in the chat. Noun.
Column header on the card in the chat. Noun.
Line under the card in the chat. {rest} lists the smaller entries.
Note under the card in the chat.
strings.en: Safe means: made again when needed. Nothing is deleted before you say OK.
strings.de: Sicher heißt: wird bei Bedarf neu erzeugt. Gelöscht wird erst nach deinem OK.

strings.context: Hermes bubble after the safe folders were deleted. {freed} is the freed space, {free} the free space now, {percent} the used share.
strings.de: Ich habe {freed} frei gemacht. Jetzt sind {free} frei ({percent} %).

strings.context: Hermes bubble: a folder was skipped. {name} is the folder, {reason} why it was skipped.
Hermes bubble before the list of folders the user decides about.
strings.en: Not touched, that is for you to decide:

strings.context: Button on the Hermes card after the run: shows the Downloads decision.
Button on the Hermes card after the run: shows old session logs.
strings.en: Show session logs older than 30 days

strings.context: Hermes bubble when nothing safe was found to delete.
strings.en: There is nothing safe to delete right now.
strings.de: Im Moment gibt es nichts Sicheres zu löschen.

strings.context: Hermes bubble when there are no merged worktrees to remove.
strings.en: There are no merged worktrees to remove.
strings.de: Es gibt keine gemergten Worktrees zu entfernen.

strings.context: Hermes bubble when measuring failed. {reason} is the system's own sentence.
strings.en: I could not measure the drive: {reason}
strings.de: Ich konnte die Platte nicht messen: {reason}

strings.context: Hermes bubble that explains one folder. {name} is the folder, {size} its size.
Hermes bubble when the model could not describe the folders; the figures are shown anyway.
strings.en: I cannot explain the folders right now, but here are the figures.
strings.de: Ich kann die Ordner gerade nicht erklären, hier sind die Zahlen.

strings.context: Verb after a key in the Hermes chat footer: deletes all safe folders.
Verb after a key in the Hermes chat footer: removes merged worktrees.
Verb after a key in the Hermes chat footer: opens the Platz tab.
